openQuestions: IS THERE A MIRROR NOTE TOKEN LIVE ON SOLANA MAINNET AT ALL, AND AT WHAT ADDRESS? Still the central gap, and now confirmed as a disclosure gap rather than a retrieval failure: republic.com/mirror, republic.com/rspax and the Republic Europe campaign page were all read on 2026-09-17 (Wayback) and none of them publishes an address. Republic states the token is "a digital representation of the Notes built on the Solana blockchain, leveraging Republic’s proprietary security token standard"; the Jupiter registry contains only impersonators. A restricted, non-tradable security token would legitimately be absent from a DEX aggregator, so this is not evidence of non-existence - but the tokenization is, from outside, entirely unaudited. NEXT STEP: ask Republic for the canonical address, then read the mint with getAccountInfo.

RESOLVED as a two-track offering, with one filing still missing. Reg CF and Reg D are not alternative accounts of one offering: the rSPAX page runs an "All US Residents" Reg CF offering via OpenDeal Portal LLC d/b/a Republic, an SEC-registered funding portal, alongside a "US Accredited & Global Investors" Rule 506(c) offering, both of the same Contingent Payout Note. The Form D on EDGAR is the 506(c) leg. WHAT REMAINS OPEN: the Reg CF panel asserts "The Issuer has filed a Form C with the ... SEC", and no Form C is on EDGAR - one CIK for RepublicX (0002080279), history D and D/A only; full-text search returns 0 hits for "rSpaceX" and 0 for "Contingent Payout Note". Was a Form C filed under another filer, withdrawn, or never filed?

ANSWERED: RepublicX holds nothing against the notes, and the obligation is funded by the issuer’s business plus a parent keepwell. "Proceeds received from note issuances are not segregated or earmarked in any way and are not required to be invested in SpaceX shares or any other specific asset"; repayment comes "from funds available to RepublicX from its business and operations and not from any dedicated pool of investor proceeds"; and the sole credit support is "that certain keepwell agreement of OpenDeal Inc., as discussed in the Offering Documents". WHAT REMAINS OPEN: the keepwell is not published - its cap, triggers, term and enforceability by noteholders are all unread, and it is now the single most important unread document in this dossier.

HOW IS THE PAYOUT CALCULATED, AND BY WHOM? Partly answered: the payout is the per-share value of SpaceX common stock at a Qualified Liquidity Event or at the 10-year maturity, "in proportion to the investment’s Reference Price of $275", with Republic’s costs inside that Reference Price. But the formula itself is only "described in the Notes and the Offering Documents", and no independent calculation agent, adjustment provision or dispute mechanism is disclosed. Obtain the Note and the subscription agreement. PARTLY ANSWERED BY THE PAGE ITSELF (Wayback capture 20260918135722): split, reverse-split and reclassification adjustments are made by "RepublicX's designated calculation agent", unnamed; the "$275 proportion" wording has been removed; the formula and any dispute mechanism remain unpublished.

ANSWERED: a Qualified Liquidity Event is "(i) an IPO or other direct listing transaction resulting in SpaceX’s equity interests being listed on a national securities exchange, (ii) a merger or acquisition of its assets or equity interests or (iii) certain other transactions resulting in a public listing or monetization of its equity interests", with dissolution named alongside IPO and acquisition in the "How it works" steps; and if none occurs the note matures at 10 years, when "Investors will receive the entire value of their repriced securities based on their pro rata share of the increase (or decrease) in the FMV of SpaceX’s common stock". Still unread: whether a tender offer, secondary round or partial acquisition qualifies, which is inside the Note’s own definition.

IS THE POST-LOCKUP SECONDARY MARKET ACTUALLY LIVE, AND DOES IT STILL MATTER? Republic "intends to allow secondary trading of Mirror Tokens after a lock-up period on one or more qualifying platforms, including INX Digital", and "RepublicX retains full discretion whether or not to list any tokens on any qualifying exchange". rSpaceX notes issued in June 2025 unlocked around June 2026; those in the Form D offering (first sale 2025-11-28) unlock around November 2026. Whether any Mirror Note has ever actually traded, where, at what price and under whose regulatory permission is unverified - and it is the test of whether this is a tokenized security or a database entry. RE-FRAMED 2026-09-18: the question is now second-order rather than first, because the exit it was a substitute for has arrived. The SpaceX IPO of June 2026 is a Qualified Liquidity Event, so the notes are due to pay out; a secondary market matters now mainly to a holder who wants out BEFORE the lock-ups and the "reasonable time period" run their course. The capability also sits inside the group: OpenDeal Inc. completed its acquisition of The INX Digital Company on 2025-11-10.

WHICH ENTITY AND WHICH REGIME APPLIES TO EUROPEAN HOLDERS? Partly answered: the campaign page states the issuer is still RepublicX LLC ("An unsecured debt security issued by RepublicX LLC", location Delaware, United States) and that the promoter is Seedrs Limited t/a Republic Europe, FCA FRN 550317, which approved the campaign as a financial promotion on 2025-09-17 and "will act as Custodian rather than provide our standard nominee service". Still open: whether the note terms, lock-up and payout are identical to the US legs, and whether the same Solana token is used. Note the size asymmetry - the UK/EU channel raised £849,170 from 850 investors against the US 506(c) leg’s $585,205 from 199.

HOW MANY MIRROR NOTE SERIES EXIST AND WHAT IS OUTSTANDING? Republic’s grid names 24 reference companies with statuses (SpaceX live; Perplexity, Anthropic and Epic Games "Filled"; the rest reservations). Only ONE offering appears on EDGAR ($3.5M offered, $585,205 sold, closed). Are the other series unfiled, filed elsewhere, offered only outside the US, or not yet launched? Is each series a separate token, and does each have its own claim on RepublicX or do they share one balance sheet? Note the answer matters more now that proceeds are known to be unsegregated and spent on general corporate purposes.

WHO ARE THE 767 HOLDERS OF THE IMPERSONATION MINT, AND DOES REPUBLIC KNOW? 79VE8a7seB6wdZaHMvhTCJUYQsWvDJPGhpZpjKsoNe9x ("rSpaceX", created within hours of the announcement) still had 767 holders on 2026-09-17, roughly four times the 199 investors in RepublicX’s actual offering. No Republic warning about impersonation mints was located on any of the three pages now read. Publishing canonical addresses would cost nothing and remains the single highest-value disclosure improvement available to this issuer.

DOES THE TOKEN STANDARD REALLY CARRY FREEZE AND CLAWBACK FOR THE MIRROR NOTES? Now less likely than the dossier assumed, not more: the "access-control ... freeze, clawback, and mint and burn" description is Republic’s own but was published for the $NOTE asset, and neither the rSPAX offering page nor the /mirror page - both read in full on 2026-09-17 - describes any token-level power over holders’ balances. What they describe is contractual restriction ("Any transfer in violation of the restrictions is void") and listing discretion. Without a mint address nothing can be confirmed, which is why forcedTransfers and reflectLegalDecisions stay "unknown".

METHODOLOGICAL NOTE FOR THE MAINTAINER: confidence was raised from "low" to "medium" on 2026-09-17 because the reason for "low" no longer holds - the issuer’s own primary pages have now been read. They were still HTTP 403 (Cloudflare, consistent with a geographic block) to curl with a browser UA and to WebFetch, but the Internet Archive was up, so republic.com/mirror, republic.com/rspax and europe.republic.com/rspax-mirror-notes were read from Wayback snapshots dated 2025-10-12, 2025-09-16 and 2025-10-07. Those snapshots are a year old at the point of reading, so anything time-sensitive on them should be re-read from a US IP before grading. The SEC filings, the Republic Core Form C-AR and the Solana registry reads are first-hand and current.

WHICH REFERENCE PRICE BASIS APPLIES AFTER THE SPLIT - $275 OR $55? SpaceX effected a five-for-one forward stock split on 2026-05-04 (424B4, Note 1), after the rSPAX notes were issued and five weeks before the IPO priced at $135.00. The payout is "a pro rata portion of the value of a common share of SpaceX at that time based on the payout formula described in the Notes and the Offering Documents", measured "in proportion to the investment’s Reference Price of $275". If that $275 is split-adjusted to $55 the note is deep in the money; if it is not, it is far out of it - a roughly fivefold difference in what a holder receives. Nothing published mentions splits, reverse splits, spin-offs, rights issues or reclassifications at all, and the only adjustment the issuer does discuss (dilution) is answered against the holder with no anti-dilution provision. A related unknown from the same event: SpaceX now has Class A and Class B common stock with different votes plus a Class C Reclassification effected at the IPO, so which class "a common share of SpaceX" means is also unstated. NEXT STEP: obtain the Note and the subscription agreement, or ask RepublicX in terms whether the Reference Price is split-adjusted. UPDATE (Wayback capture 20260918135722): the page now says "Certain anti-dilution adjustments will be made to account for splits and similar events affecting the securities of SpaceX" and hands the decision to "RepublicX's designated calculation agent", so an adjustment mechanism exists on paper; it still does not say whether the $275 Reference Price has been split-adjusted. The question stands.

IS THE CREDIT SUPPORT A KEEPWELL OR A GUARANTEE? The rSPAX page names it both ways, in two adjacent disclaimer blocks on the same page: "aside from that certain keepwell agreement of OpenDeal Inc., as discussed in the Offering Documents" and "aside from the associated guarantee of OpenDeal Inc." The difference is the whole of what the support is worth to a holder - a keepwell is a parent undertaking to keep a subsidiary solvent, frequently unenforceable by creditors, while a guarantee is a direct payment obligation owed to them. Neither instrument is published, so the cap, the triggers, the term, whether it survives a change of control of OpenDeal and whether noteholders can enforce it are all unread. This is the single most important unread document in the dossier and it does not even have a settled name.

ARE THE PROCEEDS EARMARKED OR NOT? The two Republic pages describing the same note say the opposite. republic.com/rspax: "Proceeds received from note issuances are not segregated or earmarked in any way and are not required to be invested in SpaceX shares or any other specific asset", spent on "general corporate purposes". The earlier page at republic.com/r-spax: "Proceeds are not managed collectively, are tied in each instance to individual Notes issued to investors, and are applicable solely to this specific opportunity." The dossier documents the first as the operative statement because it is the primary offering page, and records the second so the contradiction is visible - but which one governed for a given investor depends on which page they bought from, and that is a difference between an unsecured claim on a whole operating business and something closer to a tracked pool. It matters more now that a payout is actually due.

DOES THE NOTE PAY OUT IF THE REFERENCE COMPANY IS WOUND UP? "Dissolves" appears twice in the rSPAX marketing - "If SpaceX goes public, gets acquired, or dissolves, RepublicX pays you based on SpaceX’s share price at that time" and again in the "What exactly am I buying?" FAQ - but NOT in the formal definition, which names an IPO or direct listing, "a merger or acquisition of its assets or equity interests", and "certain other transactions resulting in a public listing or monetization of its equity interests". A dissolution is none of those on its face. So on the definition the note may not accelerate on the reference company’s failure at all, and a holder would wait out the ten-year maturity to be told the shares are worthless. Academic for SpaceX today; not academic for the other 23 reference companies in the grid. The answer is inside the Note’s own definition of Qualified Liquidity Event, which is not public.

Solana mainnet / registry reads by rwa-sonar on 2026-09-16: Jupiter token-registry searches for rSPAX, rSpaceX, rOPENAI, rANTHROPIC and 'Mirror' returned no genuine RepublicX instrument, only legacy-SPL and Token-2022 launchpad memecoins. NO Solana JSON-RPC read of any Mirror Note mint was possible because no address was found.

keyGovernance.evidence: No mint address is published by RepublicX in any SEC filing, press release or accessible page, and none was located in the token registries, so no authority key could be read from the chain (stocks/findings.md, Republic Mirror entry). Republic describes its own standard as carrying freeze, clawback, mint and burn functions, but nothing ties those powers to an identified key. keyGovernance.rebase is 'unknown' for the same single reason as the other three: no mint address is published, so no scaledUiAmountConfig extension — and therefore no rebase authority, and not even whether the extension exists — could be read from Solana mainnet. On paper, no programme document reserves a power to move or freeze a holder's tokens: the Private Placement Risk Disclosure says "The loss of one or more of such private keys will result in the loss of the holder’s digital Securities.", the rSPAX offering page restricts transfers only contractually, and the Terms of Service say of the Republic Wallet "At no time will we be able to access or transfer your funds without your consent." That leaves the clawback in Republic's description of its token standard unreconciled with its own offering documents until a mint can be read.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: Nothing states or implies that the chain is the legal record, and the structure argues against it. This is an unsecured note of a private Delaware LLC: the obligation exists under the note agreement and the holder's entitlement is recorded on RepublicX's own books. There is no transfer agent, no registrar and no register of any kind disclosed; transfers are locked for 12 months and then permitted only inside Republic's own permissioned secondary market; and the token standard is described as giving RepublicX freeze, clawback, mint and burn powers over holders' balances. A ledger the issuer can rewrite at will, gating a claim documented off-chain, is a convenience layer. Note also the asymmetry with the equity cases: for a registered share there is at least a contest between a transfer agent's register and the chain. Here there is no competing register to point to — which means the on-chain balance is not authoritative and nothing else is published either.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: The most restricted of the three issuers examined, on three independent grounds. (1) An absolute 12-month prohibition: 'Mirror Tokens are locked from resale or transfer for 12 months after issuance' — this follows from the Securities Act resale restrictions attaching to both Reg CF and Rule 506(c) securities, so it holds whichever exemption actually applied. (2) After unlock, transfer is not free but confined to Republic's own permissioned venue: 'Republic intends to allow trading of tokens on the Republic Secondary Market with other investors' — note 'intends to', and note that whether the venue is live for Mirror Notes is unverified. (3) Token-level access control: Republic's Solana security-token standard is described as having 'access-control functions, meaning only pre-approved wallets can receive or send tokens'. Caveat on the evidence: none of this could be verified on-chain because no mint address was found, and the access-control description was given for Republic's $NOTE asset and inferred to the Mirror Tokens.

bearerRedemption.reason: There is no redemption at all, let alone bearer redemption. No put right and no holder-initiated exit exists. Payment happens only if and when a qualifying liquidity event occurs at the referenced private company — 'When a qualifying liquidity event occurs, RepublicX will distribute the fair value of common shares of the company' — and Republic itself warns 'There is no guarantee that the company will ever conduct an IPO' and that 'the timing or likelihood of a liquidity event is not guaranteed'. Presenting the token to any third party gets nothing: no third party has any obligation under it, least of all the referenced company, which 'has not reviewed, endorsed, or participated in this offering in any capacity'.

forcedTransfers.reason: Claimed elsewhere, absent here, and unverifiable either way. Republic describes its Solana security-token standard as including "freeze, clawback, and mint and burn functions to ensure legally compliant trading", which would supply the mechanism for court-ordered seizure, theft recovery, loss recovery and inheritance. Three problems prevent scoring it "yes", one of them new. First, that description was published for Republic’s own $NOTE asset rather than for the Mirror Notes. Second, and new as of 2026-09-17: the rSPAX offering page and the /mirror page were both read in full and neither describes any freeze, clawback, burn or forced-transfer power over the tokens - what they describe is contractual, exemption-driven transfer restriction ("Any transfer in violation of the restrictions is void") and listing discretion. So the inference is weaker than before, not stronger. Third and decisively, no mint address was located, so nothing could be checked against Solana mainnet - unlike Bullish and Securitize, where the permanent delegate and freeze authority were read directly off the mint. Recorded as unknown on the principle that an unverified capability is not a capability, and note that even if present the powers would sit with a single private LLC with no named role, no disclosed policy and no regulated registrar.

titleDeed.reason: Emphatically not, and the issuer says so. The token conveys no ownership of the referenced company: it 'offers economic exposure to SpaceX through blockchain without giving equity or ownership rights' and 'does not represent actual ownership or equity in SpaceX'. What the holder has is a derived, contingent, unsecured contractual claim against RepublicX LLC — a debt note whose payout references a third party's share value. Nor is it a title to anything RepublicX holds, since the note is unsecured and no backing asset is even disclosed. This is the cleanest 'no' in the set and the structural difference from the Bullish and Securitize dossiers, where the token IS the registered share.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Not established, but the evidence is now two-sided rather than absent. The offering page requires a platform wallet - "To receive Tokens, investors will be required to create a Republic Wallet", "Yes, a Republic Wallet is required in order to participate in these offerings and to receive Tokens" - and pays out "to the Investor’s verified Republic Wallet". The /mirror marketing page claims the opposite emphasis: "Investments custodied in your own wallets, trackable on blockchain, backed by Republic." Nothing states whether a Republic Wallet is self-custodial or hosted, and the UK/EU channel is plainly not self-custody at all: "If you invest in this Campaign, Seedrs will act as Custodian rather than provide our standard nominee service." With no mint address the distribution of holdings across accounts cannot be inspected either. Left unknown rather than guessed. STRENGTHENED BUT STILL UNKNOWN (2026-09-18): the Terms of Service now supply a flat statement on the custody side - "THE REPUBLIC WALLET IS NON - CUSTODIAL . Republic does not store or transmit digital assets" and "At no time will we be able to access or transfer your funds without your consent" (§IX.2, spacing as printed). Three reasons that does not settle the field, which is why the value stays "unknown". (1) Context: §IX.2 is headed "Republic Note and Wallet" and describes a wallet built on "the Algorand blockchain service platform" and "powered through our partnership with independent third parties, Comakery (dba Upside)" - not Solana, and not the Mirror Notes. (2) The same section contemplates the opposite in the next breath: "for regulatory and risk reasons, as determined by Republic Core in its sole discretion, certain prohibitions or restrictions may apply to your Republic Notes and/or other digital assets and may be hardwired into the Republic Wallet or otherwise limited." (3) With no mint address published, nothing can be checked on-chain. On the other side the offering page still requires a platform wallet to receive tokens and pays out "to the Investor’s verified Republic Wallet", and the UK/EU leg is plainly not self-custody at all. UPDATE (Wayback capture 20260918130544 of republic.com/mirror): the "Investments custodied in your own wallets" bullet has been removed; /mirror now says only "Republic issues tokens in your Republic wallets", and the offering page adds refunds to what is paid into the Republic Wallet. Still unknown.

issuerIndependent.reason: Total dependence on a single counterparty, and more so than in any other structure examined. RepublicX LLC is a Delaware LLC formed in 2025 with no disclosed capital, no transfer agent, no trustee, no collateral and no independent calculation agent. If it disappears the token means nothing: the payout is its unsecured promise, the 'fair value' determination is its own, the secondary market is its affiliate's, and the token's transferability depends on its access-control keys. The Form D shows an entity that raised $585,205 and closed the offering early ('We do not intend to sell the remaining'), against notes whose eventual payout could be many multiples of subscription value if the referenced company appreciates — with nothing located to indicate how that obligation would be funded. Compare the equity cases: there, the SHARE survives the platform's failure even when the TOKEN does not. Here, nothing survives.

presetJurisdiction.reason: The applicable legal framework is identifiable even though the instrument's own terms were not readable: a Delaware LLC with New York offices, a US federal securities exemption claimed on the public record (Form D, Rule 506(c), file no. 021-565769), a named manager (OpenDeal Inc.) and a named signatory (Jeffrey Vier), with a separate and clearly demarcated UK/EU channel through Republic Europe. A US holder would know which courts and which regulator to approach. Marked 'yes' on that basis, but with two real qualifications: the governing-law clause of the note itself is unread because the offering pages are geo-blocked; and the regulatory characterisation is internally contradicted — marketed as Reg CF, filed as Reg D 506(c) — so which exemption governs the securities-law treatment of any given holder's notes is genuinely unclear.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Nothing independent exists anywhere in the structure, and this is the most complete absence in the set. No transfer agent, no trustee, no custodian, no auditor report on the notes, no proof-of-reserve, no NAV or valuation publication, no independent calculation agent, no smart-contract audit, no published mint address and no on-chain metadata to attach anything to. Every fact about the instrument — its backing, its value, its outstanding amount, its holder list — is RepublicX's unverified assertion. The referenced companies explicitly disclaim involvement, which removes the one party who could authenticate the economic reference.

aiReady.reason: Fails on every limb. Transfers are prohibited outright for 12 months, then restricted to a permissioned affiliate venue among vetted investors; the token standard is described as permitting only pre-approved wallets to send or receive; and subscription runs through a retail investment platform's KYC/AML onboarding with per-investor purchase caps ($5,000 initial), which is exactly the kind of identity and suitability gate an autonomous agent cannot pass. Fails on unconditionalTransfers regardless.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: Cannot be established. The mechanism may exist — Republic's token standard is described as including freeze and clawback — but it is unverified on-chain and only inferred to apply to the Mirror Notes, and no contractual undertaking to honour judicial or regulatory orders was readable, because the note agreement and offering pages could not be retrieved. There is also no regulated intermediary in the structure carrying such obligations by operation of law: no transfer agent means no Exchange Act §17A duties, no Rule 17Ad-17 lost-holder obligations and no escheat process. Note the countervailing point that keeps this from being a 'no': a plain unsecured note of a Delaware LLC is an ordinary contractual claim that US courts can adjudicate and garnish by conventional means — the legal system can reach the CLAIM even if nobody can demonstrate it can reach the TOKEN.

meetingOfMinds.reason: Buyer-and-seller agreement is worth nothing here for a full year, and little after. For 12 months no transfer is permitted on any terms. Afterwards, Republic 'intends to allow' trading on its own secondary market among vetted investors, with pre-approved wallets on the token side — so the counterparty set, the venue and the permission all sit with the issuer's group, not with the parties. Two willing counterparties cannot effect a valid transfer of a Mirror Note by agreeing to one. UPDATE (Wayback captures 20260918130544 and 20260918135722): /mirror no longer advertises trading "on the Republic secondary market"; its FAQ keeps the 12-month lock and the "intends to allow" wording, and the offering page now fixes one-year resale limits and says "investors should not expect a secondary market to develop". Value unchanged.

You have no right whatsoever to equity in SpaceX, RepublicX, or Republic by virtue of investing in any offering", and "Investors’ respective creditor rights do not consist of any shareholders’ rights". Reinforced by an unusually thorough eight-limb affiliation disclaimer: "SpaceX has not reviewed, approved, authorized, endorsed, sponsored, or consented to any aspect of this security, token, marketing material, or transaction structure."

findings.statement: RepublicX publishes no mint address in any SEC filing, press release or retrievable page, so no outside party can audit the token's supply, extensions, authorities or holder distribution, and the ticker namespace has been captured by impersonators. The top Solana result for 'rSpaceX' is 79VE8a7seB6wdZaHMvhTCJUYQsWvDJPGhpZpjKsoNe9x, a legacy-SPL one-billion-supply pump.fun token created on the announcement day with 768 holders - roughly four times the 199 investors in the actual closed offering.

findings.statement: Marketed and filed exemptions do not line up because one filing is missing, not because they conflict: the rSPAX page runs a Reg CF offering ("All US Residents", via OpenDeal Portal LLC d/b/a Republic, an SEC-registered funding portal, $50-$5,000) beside a Rule 506(c) offering ("US Accredited & Global Investors"), and only the 506(c) leg is on EDGAR (Form D, item 06c, hasNonAccreditedInvestors false, 199 investors, $585,205 of $3,500,000, closed). The Reg CF panel asserts "The Issuer has filed a Form C" with the SEC; EDGAR holds no Form C for the filer, and full-text search returns zero hits for "rSpaceX" and zero for "Contingent Payout Note". Reg CF requires a Form C before any offer.

findings.statement: RepublicX LLC has filed no offering circular (Form 1-A), no Form C offering statement, no registration statement and no periodic report. Its entire filing history is two Form D notices, which are 15-question notices of sale carrying no risk factors, no financial statements and no description of the instrument.

findings.statement: The holder's claim is an unsecured obligation of RepublicX LLC itself, a Delaware LLC formed in 2025 whose manager is the Republic group parent. There is no SPV, trust, segregation or ring-fence; any assets RepublicX may hold to hedge are neither disclosed nor pledged, so on insolvency holders would rank with general creditors over a pool whose contents are unknown.

findings.statement: No custodian, trustee or collateral agent is named anywhere, and the reason is now on the record rather than inferred: there is nothing to custody. "Proceeds received from note issuances are not segregated or earmarked in any way and are not required to be invested in SpaceX shares or any other specific asset", and the notes are repaid "from funds available to RepublicX from its business and operations and not from any dedicated pool of investor proceeds". So "mirror" is a payout formula, not a backed position. The only custodian anywhere in the structure is on the UK/EU channel, where Seedrs Limited "will act as Custodian rather than provide our standard nominee service" for the investment position itself.

findings.statement: The sole determinant of what a holder receives is RepublicX's own determination of the per-share value of the reference company at a Qualified Liquidity Event or at the 10-year maturity, in USD or USDC, under a payout formula published nowhere. No independent calculation agent, no valuation methodology and no dispute mechanism. UPDATE (offering page, Wayback capture 2026-09-18): the page now promises anti-dilution adjustments for splits, reverse splits and reclassifications, made by "RepublicX's designated calculation agent" — an agent designated by the debtor and not named, so the adjustment is still the payer's own determination. The split point is no longer hypothetical: SpaceX effected a five-for-one forward split on 2026-05-04, after issuance, and nothing says whether the $275 Reference Price is split-adjusted. The party that owes the money still decides how much is owed.

findings.statement: No NAV, mark, indicative value or valuation methodology is published at any cadence. For a structured note this is the product, and it is unreadable.

findings.statement: No oracle, feed, NAV or mark of any kind is published for the Mirror Notes, so the "mirror" is an intention rather than an enforced tracking mechanism. the reason given for it - "The referenced companies are private, so there is no market price to feed" - has stopped being true of rSPAX. SpaceX priced its IPO at $135.00 a share on 2026-06-12 and trades on Nasdaq as "SPCX", so a continuous public price now exists and is not fed anywhere: there is still no oracle, no published mark and no NAV, and the payout is still computed off an unpublished formula by the issuer. The absence is therefore now a disclosure choice rather than a structural impossibility.

findings.statement: Investors subscribe through the Republic platform with per-investor caps, which entails identity verification, and the filed Rule 506(c) exemption requires reasonable steps to verify accredited status. findings.statement: Republic maintains public product and offering pages carrying substantive terms, and they are unreachable from outside the US: republic.com/mirror, republic.com/rspax and europe.republic.com/rspax-mirror-notes returned HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) to curl with a browser user agent and to WebFetch on both 2026-09-16 and 2026-09-17. On 2026-09-17 the Internet Archive was up, so all three were read from Wayback snapshots (20251012164756, 20250916201851, 20251007111149). The limitation is therefore geographic availability and staleness, not absence: a reader outside the US cannot read the live terms of a security they hold, and the newest snapshot available was about eleven months old.

keyGovernance.evidence: No mint address is published by RepublicX in any SEC filing, press release or accessible page, and none was located in the token registries, so no authority key could be read from the chain (stocks/findings.md, Republic Mirror entry). Republic describes its own standard as carrying freeze, clawback, mint and burn functions, but nothing ties those powers to an identified key. keyGovernance.rebase is 'unknown' for the same single reason as the other three: no mint address is published, so no scaledUiAmountConfig extension — and therefore no rebase authority, and not even whether the extension exists — could be read from Solana mainnet. On paper, no programme document reserves a power to move or freeze a holder's tokens: the Private Placement Risk Disclosure says "The loss of one or more of such private keys will result in the loss of the holder’s digital Securities.", the rSPAX offering page restricts transfers only contractually, and the Terms of Service say of the Republic Wallet "At no time will we be able to access or transfer your funds without your consent." That leaves the clawback in Republic's description of its token standard unreconciled with its own offering documents until a mint can be read.

links.label: Ownership of the underlying

fields.value: A SENIOR UNSECURED DEBT CLAIM ON REPUBLICX LLC, with a parent keepwell behind it and nothing else. The instrument is named on the offering page: "You are purchasing tokenized interests in Contingent Payout Notes (each, a “Note”, and if multiple “Notes”), a debt security (i.e., payment obligation) issued by RepublicX". It bears no interest ("There is no periodic interest on the Notes"), matures 10 years from issuance, and pays "a pro rata portion of the value of a common share of SpaceX at that time" on the earlier of maturity or a Qualified Liquidity Event. On default: "the entire unpaid principal of the Securities shall become immediately due and payable at the option of the Investor. As senior unsecured creditors of RepublicX LLC, Investors’ claims to the assets of RepublicX LLC will have priority over those of RepublicX LLC’s equity holders." REPUBLICX HOLDS NOTHING AGAINST IT, and says so: "Proceeds received from note issuances are not segregated or earmarked in any way and are not required to be invested in SpaceX shares or any other specific asset. Instead, offering proceeds are used for RepublicX’s general corporate purposes", and the notes are "subject to repayment from funds available to RepublicX from its business and operations and not from any dedicated pool of investor proceeds". The one piece of credit support is a parent undertaking whose terms are not published: "Your sole counterparty is RepublicX LLC, which alone, aside from that certain keepwell agreement of OpenDeal Inc., as discussed in the Offering Documents, is responsible for all payment and reporting obligations under the Notes." The holder owns no share, no equity, no fund unit and no interest in any SPV: "You have no right whatsoever to equity in SpaceX, RepublicX, or Republic by virtue of investing in any offering." The referenced company is not a party.

NONE, now on the issuer’s own words rather than by inference. The rSPAX offering page states that "Proceeds received from note issuances are not segregated or earmarked in any way and are not required to be invested in SpaceX shares or any other specific asset", that proceeds go to "RepublicX’s general corporate purposes ... primarily technology and product development, platform and operating costs (including services from affiliates), payroll, and related working capital, and may be reallocated in management’s discretion", and that the notes are repaid "from funds available to RepublicX from its business and operations and not from any dedicated pool of investor proceeds". So there is no custodian, trustee, collateral agent or SPV because there is nothing to custody. The only party holding anything for investors sits on the UK/EU channel, where "Seedrs will act as Custodian rather than provide our standard nominee service" - a custodian of the investment position on Republic Europe’s books, not of any SpaceX exposure.

links.label: Issuance and redemption

fields.value: There is no redemption at the holder’s option and no put right. Payment falls due on the EARLIER of a QUALIFYING LIQUIDITY EVENT of the referenced company or a 10-YEAR MATURITY: "Payouts, if any, occur within a reasonable time period (as further described in the offering documentation) after the earlier of the maturity date (i.e., 10 years from the date of issuance) or a Qualified Liquidity Event, plus the expiration of any applicable lock-up period(s)." A Qualified Liquidity Event is defined as "(i) an IPO or other direct listing transaction resulting in SpaceX’s equity interests being listed on a national securities exchange, (ii) a merger or acquisition of its assets or equity interests or (iii) certain other transactions resulting in a public listing or monetization of its equity interests"; dissolution is named alongside IPO and acquisition in the "How it works" steps. If no event occurs, the note still resolves: "On the Maturity Date, Investors will receive the entire value of their repriced securities based on their pro rata share of the increase (or decrease) in the FMV of SpaceX’s common stock." Republic still warns "There is no guarantee of returns, and the timing or likelihood of a liquidity event is not guaranteed", and "No payout of any amount, including your principal investment amount, is guaranteed." UPDATE (2026-09-18): THE TRIGGER HAS FIRED. SpaceX registered its Class A common stock under the Exchange Act on 2026-06-10 and priced its IPO at $135.00 a share in a prospectus filed 2026-06-12, listing on Nasdaq and Nasdaq Texas as "SPCX" - squarely "an IPO or other direct listing transaction resulting in SpaceX’s equity interests being listed on a national securities exchange" on the definition quoted above. So the field above should no longer be read as describing a contingency: payment is now due under this clause, and the whole of what stands between a holder and it is "a reasonable time period", "any applicable lock-up period(s)" - the IPO’s own extended lock-up runs to the second trading day after SpaceX’s Q2 2027 results, with staged early releases from Q1 2027 - and an unpublished payout formula whose Reference Price basis is itself ambiguous after the 2026-05-04 five-for-one split. Nothing located shows a payment has been made to any holder. UPDATE (Wayback capture 20260918135722 of republic.com/rspax, read 2026-09-23; no capture exists between 20250916201851 and this one, and the same wording was already on republic.com/rspax2 in its capture 20260221005623): the Qualified Liquidity Event definition now lists examples - "(e.g. SPAC merger, restructuring, bankruptcy proceeding, tender offer, recapitalization) resulting in a public listing or monetization of SpaceX equity" - so a bankruptcy proceeding and a tender offer are expressly triggers, and the maturity is now dated: "On the Maturity Date (November 3, 2035) within 30 calendar days".

At maturity or a qualifying liquidity event, "RepublicX pays you based on SpaceX’s share price at that time––the Redemption Price––in proportion to the investment’s Reference Price of $275", and the holder picks the settlement asset: "Each Investor will have the choice of receiving payouts in either (1) U.S. dollars or (2) USDC (U.S. Dollar Coin) to the Investor’s verified Republic Wallet, or such other stablecoin of the Issuer's choosing in the Issuer's sole discretion in the event that USDC is not industry standard at the time payment is due." The payout formula itself is only "described in the Notes and the Offering Documents", which are not public, and no independent calculation agent or dispute mechanism is disclosed. Before then, the only route out is secondary sale: tokens are "locked from resale or transfer for 12 months after issuance", after which "Republic intends to allow secondary trading of Mirror Tokens after a lock-up period on one or more qualifying platforms, including INX Digital" - but "RepublicX retains full discretion whether or not to list any tokens on any qualifying exchange." UPDATE (Wayback capture 20260918135722 of republic.com/rspax, read 2026-09-23; no capture exists between 20250916201851 and this one, and the same wording was already on republic.com/rspax2 in its capture 20260221005623): the settlement choice now reads "(1) U.S. dollars or (2) USDC (U.S. Dollar Coin), or another stablecoin chosen by the Issuer", so the issuer may substitute a stablecoin without USDC having ceased to be industry standard; the "How it works" step with the $275 proportion is gone ("Upon a qualifying liquidity event, investors may receive payouts in USD or USDC, as outlined in the offering documents."); split and reclassification adjustments are made by "RepublicX's designated calculation agent" - the obligor's own, unnamed; and the venue sentence now reads "rSPAX tokens are designed to be tradable on INX, a regulated digital securities trading venue, subject to market conditions and eligibility."

Disclosed in architecture, undisclosed in amount. "All fees reduce your net return. Fees here include a premium built into the Reference Price as well as other fees associated with the Republic platform. In the event secondary trading exists on any qualifying exchange, there may also be fees associated therewith." The premium is inside the $275 Reference Price rather than charged separately - "Republic’s costs are baked into the Reference Price, meaning the bar for making a profit is higher" - and "Investors’ entitlement is reduced/adjusted by fees". No rate, schedule or percentage is published anywhere located; the only hard number in the structure is what the issuer pays its own affiliate: Republic Core receives "an initial onboarding fee of $150,000 and ongoing quarterly fees of $75,000 beginning upon the commencement of the first RX Offering" (Republic Core Form C-AR, p. 47). UPDATE (Wayback capture 20260918135722 of republic.com/rspax, read 2026-09-23; no capture exists between 20250916201851 and this one, and the same wording was already on republic.com/rspax2 in its capture 20260221005623): the "Republic’s costs are baked into the Reference Price" bullet was removed with the old "How it works" section (the FAQ fee answer is unchanged), and the maturity payout is now "subject to adjustments for applicable costs or taxes".

fields.value: UNVERIFIED ON-CHAIN - no mint address was found, so none of the following could be confirmed against Solana mainnet. What is stated, now from the issuer’s own offering page rather than press: (1) a hard 12-month lock - "Mirror Tokens are locked from resale or transfer for 12 months after issuance"; (2) exemption-driven restrictions with a nullity sanction - "There are transfer restrictions based upon the applicable exemption the Notes and any beneficial interests are issued thereunder, including Rule 506 resale limitations, Regulation S distribution-compliance periods and U.S. person restrictions, if applicable. Any transfer in violation of the restrictions is void."; (3) after unlock, transfer only on venues Republic chooses - "on one or more qualifying platforms, including INX Digital", "subject to the applicable rules and limitations on transferability including, without limitation, KYC/AML of the investor", and "RepublicX retains full discretion whether or not to list any tokens on any qualifying exchange"; (4) delivery only into a platform wallet - "To receive Tokens, investors will be required to create a Republic Wallet." fields.value: None flow to the holder, by design - this is a note referencing a company that is not a party to it. No dividend, distribution, voting, proxy, information or inspection right in the referenced company attaches: "You will not receive dividends or other distributions from SpaceX and will have no rights to vote or influence SpaceX’s management and must rely solely on public information, which may be limited, incomplete, or stale." The ONE adjustment question the issuer does address it answers against the holder: "Because the Notes track the value of common shares on a price per share basis, their return may be reduced if SpaceX issues additional shares or equity-linked securities, which could dilute the value of each share" - i.e. dilution risk is borne by the holder with no anti-dilution adjustment. The referenced company’s other corporate actions matter only as inputs to the eventual per-share value, and nothing located explains how a stock split, recapitalisation, down-round, secondary tender, partial acquisition, SPAC merger or reclassification would be treated, nor what happens if a liquidity event is for a different share class than the one referenced. A 10-year maturity does now bound the open-endedness. On the RepublicX side no freeze, clawback, mint or burn power is described on the offering pages at all - that description belongs to Republic’s own $NOTE material. UPDATE (Wayback capture 20260918135722 of republic.com/rspax, read 2026-09-23; no capture exists between 20250916201851 and this one, and the same wording was already on republic.com/rspax2 in its capture 20260221005623): SUPERSEDES "no anti-dilution adjustment" and "nothing located explains how a stock split … would be treated": the page now says "Certain anti-dilution adjustments will be made to account for splits and similar events affecting the securities of SpaceX." and "If SpaceX declares a stock split, reverse stock split or other reclassification of its common stock, RepublicX's designated calculation agent will determine whether that event has a diluting or concentrative effect on the theoretical value of the common shares of SpaceX and, if so, will make such calculations and adjustments to the terms of the Notes as may be necessary". The agent is RepublicX's own and unnamed, no method is published, and dilution by new issuance is still borne by the holder.

fields.value: THREE EXEMPTIONS CLAIMED ON ONE PAGE FOR THE SAME NOTE, one of whose filings cannot be found (the page’s own Important Disclosures block adds a Regulation S leg, recorded as (5) below). The rSPAX offering page presents them side by side. (1) "All US Residents" - Regulation CF: "This securities offering is being conducted pursuant to the exemption from registration afforded under Section 4(a)(6) of the Securities Act of 1933 (“Regulation Crowdfunding”)", "conducted by RepublicX, LLC (the “Issuer”) via OpenDeal Portal LLC d/b/a Republic, an SEC registered funding portal", minimum $50, maximum $5,000, intermediary "Republic Funding Portal". (2) "US Accredited & Global Investors" - Rule 506(c): "Under Regulation D, participation is limited to verified accredited investors in the United States", minimum $50, no broker-dealer involved ("No broker-dealer registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”), the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (“FINRA”), or any state securities regulator is participating in, or has otherwise passed upon or approved this offering") and no SIPC protection. So the Form D on EDGAR - exemption item 06c, security type DEBT, first sale 2025-11-28, $585,205 of $3,500,000 sold, 199 investors, hasNonAccreditedInvestors FALSE, offering closed - is the 506(c) leg, and the accredited-only data is consistent rather than contradictory. THE REMAINING PROBLEM IS A MISSING FILING, NOT A MISMATCHED ONE: the Reg CF panel states "The Issuer has filed a Form C with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”), which contains important information about this offering and its risks", and no Form C exists. EDGAR company search returns exactly one CIK for "RepublicX" (0002080279) whose complete filing history is Form D and Form D/A; EDGAR full-text search returns 4 hits for "RepublicX" (those two filings plus two Republic Core LLC Form C-ARs), 0 for "rSpaceX" and 0 for "Contingent Payout Note". Separately, the /mirror page’s "rule 206 of Regulation CF" citation is a testing-the-waters reservation notice, not the offering itself: it says in terms that "No investment commitments can be accepted and no funds can be received unless the issuer files a Form C with the SEC and starts accepting investments." (3) NOT A REGISTERED SECURITY on any view: no registration statement, no exchange listing, no transfer agent. (4) The UK/EU channel is separately regulated: the rSPAX Mirror Notes campaign on Republic Europe was "approved by Seedrs Limited (trading as Republic Europe) ... as of 17 September 2025 as a financial promotion", and Republic Europe "is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority with firm reference number 550317". (5) A THIRD EXEMPTION, MISSED BY THE EARLIER PASSES: below the two offering panels, the rSPAX page’s "Important Disclosures" block describes "two separate, concurrent offerings" of its own - a Regulation D leg and a "Regulation S Offering – Conducted pursuant to Regulation S under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended. Under Regulation S, the securities may only be offered and sold outside the United States to non-“U.S. persons” (as defined in Rule 902(k) under the Securities Act)." Regulation S securities "have not been and will not be registered under the Securities Act or the securities laws of any U.S. state, and may not be resold or otherwise transferred in the United States absent registration or an available exemption", and the transfer-restriction FAQ names "Regulation S distribution-compliance periods and U.S. person restrictions" alongside the Rule 506 resale limits. So one page claims Section 4(a)(6) Regulation Crowdfunding in one panel, Rule 506(c) in the other and Regulation S in the disclosures, while EDGAR holds only the Form D for the 506(c) leg; and the page’s two accounts of how many concurrent offerings there are do not agree with each other either. Note also that transferRestrictions.usPersonsExcluded is recorded as false for this dossier, which is right for the Reg CF and 506(c) legs and wrong for the Reg S leg - the same note is sold on both bases.

US federal securities law for the two exempt offerings (Reg CF s.4(a)(6) and Rule 506(c) - see regulatoryStatus) plus, presumably, Delaware LLC law and New York law for the note instrument. PARTLY VERIFIED NOW: republic.com and europe.republic.com still return HTTP 403 (Cloudflare) from this host, but the Internet Archive was reachable on 2026-09-17, so the offering pages have been read from Wayback snapshots. That yields the exemptions, the payout formula and Reference Price, the 10-year maturity, the Qualified Liquidity Event definition, the acceleration remedy on an Event of Default, the senior-unsecured ranking, the keepwell agreement of OpenDeal Inc., the fee architecture and the transfer restrictions. What is STILL unread is the note itself: the subscription agreement, the Note, the payout formula in full, the keepwell terms and the governing-law clause of the instrument are all "described in the Notes and the Offering Documents", which are behind the investment checkout.

issuers.name: Securitize SECZ
issuers.issuerText: Securitize Corp. (NYSE: SECZ) — the securities issuer is the listed company itself (Delaware corporation, SEC CIK 0002094496), which is also its own tokenization platform, its own SEC-registered DIGITAL transfer agent (Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC) and the operator of the broker-dealer/ATS that gates access. Vertical integration is the defining feature of the tokenization layer — the platform that mints, the venue that gates access, the whitelist, the control book and every on-chain authority are all one corporate group. It does NOT extend to the register of record: the S-1 and the 424B3 Description of Securities say "The Transfer Agent for the Securitize Common Stock is Continental Stock Transfer & Trust Company", and Securitize's own tokenization instructions say the same with the operational detail attached ("DRS & DWAC #: 7808"). So the share register sits with an independent third party — carried through from the CEPT SPAC, whose transfer agent and trustee Continental was — while Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC keeps the tokenized sub-register. That is a materially better position than this dossier asserted until 2026-09-18, and it puts SECZ alongside Superstate (independent Recordkeeping Transfer Agent) and Bullish (Equiniti, third party until Q1 2027) rather than apart from them.
chains: Avalanche (larger deployment per the S-1; contract not verified here)

Securitize states native integration with 21 chains — Ethereum, Avalanche, Polygon, Optimism, Arbitrum, XDC, Base, InkChain, ZkSync, Mantle, Hedera, BNB, Linea, Sei, Tron, Aptos, Solana, XRP Ledger, Cronos, Injective and SUI — with 'Tokenization on other blockchains ... being explored' for SECZ specifically
products: Tokenized SECZ — 'a natively tokenized version of our common stock', enabled on the Closing Date of the business combination (2026-07-01) and live from the NYSE listing (2026-07-02), issued on Solana and Avalanche. 'Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class.'

Solana deployment — Token-2022 mint 5VzwKkvynPJzcgwhBe7ESEyNgqMbo15yBu7Sehssd9ED, created 2026-06-29, supply 148,998 tokens across 117 token accounts on 2026-09-16. 'Trading of Tokenized SECZ on Solana is now enabled via on-chain liquidity provision partners.'

Avalanche deployment — the larger of the two; 'certain shares of Tokenized SECZ on Avalanche are held by persons who have executed lock-up agreements pursuant to terms of the Business Combination Agreement'. Contract address not verified by rwa-sonar (out of Solana scope).
Announced follow-on (2026-08-20 press reporting, unverified): SECZ used as collateral in Solana on-chain credit markets.

('CEPT'), Securitize, Inc. ('Old Securitize') and Securitize Holdings, Inc. under a Business Combination Agreement dated 2025-10-27, consummated 2026-07-01 after stockholder approval on 2026-06-29. NYSE listing certified 2026-07-01 (Form CERT), 8-A12B filed 2026-06-30, first trade 2026-07-02. Register maintained by Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC — SEC Transfer Agent File No. 084-06638, CIK 0001782266, with a live filing history (TA-1 through TA-1/A and annual TA-2s). Access gated by the group's SEC-registered, FINRA-member broker-dealer and ATS.
issuers.entityJurisdiction: Delaware corporation, principal operations United States. All regulated entities in the stack are SEC-registered/FINRA-member US entities.
issuers.governingLaw: Delaware General Corporation Law governs the common stock and the share register; US federal securities law governs the listing, the transfer agent (Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21) and the broker-dealer/ATS gating access. No separate token terms of service or holder agreement for Tokenized SECZ was located; the operative public instrument is the Form S-1 prospectus risk factor plus the Securitize platform's general investor terms (not located in tokenized-SECZ-specific form).
issuers.regulatoryStatus: The most heavily regulated of the three Solana-native issuers examined, and the only one where the tokenization vendor is itself the registrant. The underlying security is registered common stock of a Delaware SEC-reporting company listed on the NYSE (S-4 registration statement effective 2026-06-05; S-1 filed 2026-07-31, EFFECT 2026-08-07; 424B3 prospectuses 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-13). Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC is an SEC-registered transfer agent (File No. 084-06638). The S-1 describes the group as 'the only vertically integrated tokenization provider with SEC-registered entities across a transfer agent, broker-dealer, alternative trading system (ATS), investor advisor and fund administration'. Access to the tokenized form is intermediated by a regulated broker-dealer: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer' (note: the S-1 renders the entity name as 'Securities Markets, LLC'. RESOLVED 2026-09-17 against a primary source: Securitize's own 2026-07-02 press release names 'Securitize Markets, LLC, an SEC-registered broker-dealer and member FINRA/SIPC that operates an SEC-regulated Alternative Trading System (ATS)', so the S-1 wording is a typographical error in a registration statement and the gatekeeping broker-dealer is Securitize Markets, LLC). No exemptive relief or no-action letter for the tokenized form was located; the S-1 warns that 'market intermediaries may face unclear or evolving obligations'.
issuers.holderClaim: The holder owns the actual registered common share. The S-1 risk factor is unambiguous on two points at once: 'we enabled Tokenized SECZ, a natively tokenized version of our common stock. Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class' and 'Tokenized SECZ provides an additional mechanism for investors to hold and transfer shares in the Company'. The issuer's own press release adds that this is an 'issuer-sponsored tokenization of the same common stock trading on the NYSE' and that 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions.' Holders may move between forms: 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ'. There is no SPV, receipt or nominee layer in the legal structure — but access runs through a broker-dealer's onboarding, so whether the holder is a registered holder of record in their own name or a customer of the broker-dealer is NOT established by any document located, and this is the central unresolved question for this issuer.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: No custodian is interposed for the security itself — the token is the share and the register is Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC's master securityholder file. For its own corporate digital assets Securitize discloses self-custody via Fireblocks MPC ('enables us to retain exclusive control over the authorization of transactions without ever generating or storing a traditional private key'), and states that 'In the case of Securitize-issued tokenized securities held in self-custody utilizing Fireblocks infrastructure, Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent.' Investor-side custody may be self-custody (see transferRestrictions) or broker/custodian-held; the split is not disclosed.

custodyVerification.agent: Two transfer agents, and only the tokenized one is an affiliate. (1) Continental Stock Transfer & Trust Company — SEC transfer agent File No. 084-00034, CIK 0000024179, DRS & DWAC #7808 — is the transfer agent of record for the Securitize common stock, named in the S-1/424B3 Description of Securities and in Securitize's own tokenize instructions, and independent of the issuer. (2) Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC — SEC transfer agent File No. 084-06638, CIK 0001782266 — is the "exclusive digital transfer agent for tokenized securities issued on Securitize's platform" and keeps the control book and master securityholder file for the tokenized units; it is an affiliate of the issuer, not an independent party, and is never named in the S-1. No transfer-agency agreement for SECZ is published on either side, so the division of the books between them, and how the two are reconciled, rests on the issuer's own description.
custodyVerification.frequency: continuous, claimed — 'every transaction and ownership record is maintained on a single, verifiable ledger accessible in real time'; multichain deployments 'are managed and reconciled through the same control book and master securityholder file to ensure that total outstanding units remain consistent and singular across chains'
custodyVerification.notes: NO PUBLIC VERIFICATION FEED. Securitize publishes no instruments API, no per-token supply endpoint, no allowlist enumeration and no reconciliation report for SECZ. The token's TokenMetadata URI (https://metadata.securitize.io/secz.json) resolves but contains only name, symbol, description and image — no CUSIP/ISIN, no register link, no supply, no attestation. The Securitize Connect API (https://sec-connect-api-docs.securitize.io/wallets) documents the whitelisting mechanism but is an authenticated partner API, not a public verification surface. VERIFIED ON SOLANA MAINNET BY RWA-SONAR, 2026-09-16 (slot ~447535518): mint 5VzwKkvynPJzcgwhBe7ESEyNgqMbo15yBu7Sehssd9ED is a Token-2022 mint, decimals 6, supply 148,998.000000, name 'Securitize Corp.', symbol 'SECZ'; 117 Token-2022 accounts exist for the mint (getProgramAccounts with mint filter); extensions MetadataPointer, PausableConfig, DefaultAccountState=Frozen, PermanentDelegate, ScaledUiAmount, TokenMetadata; NO TransferHook. Authority topology, and this is the notable finding: mintAuthority == freezeAuthority == 8TwererfKZwiBfKQs2bQmVRrezqeFG3JvrVsbpGaPbQs, and getAccountInfo on that address returns null — a zero-lamport, never-initialized account, which is the signature of a program-derived address used as a CPI signer rather than a funded wallet. That is a MEANINGFULLY BETTER key posture than Bullish, whose mint/freeze authority is a plain funded wallet: it implies a Securitize program mediates minting and thawing. It is not proof — the owning program was not identified, and the separate authority on the extensions (D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA1kEzKZNrdMvYKPLdZtrmAnnK6jCS, which holds permanentDelegate, pausable, scaledUiAmount, metadataPointer and tokenMetadata update authority) was not resolved either. MEASURED CONTRADICTION: press coverage (CoinDesk, PRNewswire, RWA.xyz-sourced) reports '$295 million in tokenized shares'. The Solana mint holds 148,998 tokens, worth roughly $1.24M at the ~$8.35 price Jupiter reported on 2026-09-16 — about 0.4% of $295M. Either essentially all of the $295M sits on Avalanche (consistent with the S-1, which puts the locked-up business-combination shares there) or the $295M figure is not comparable to on-chain supply. Any grading that attributes the $295M headline to Solana is wrong by more than two orders of magnitude.

redemption.eligibility: Holders who have completed the broker-dealer onboarding: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer.' The issuer's press release adds that the tokenized form is for 'eligible U.S. investors' subject to 'onboarding, KYC/AML verification, jurisdictional eligibility checks'. Certain Avalanche holdings are additionally subject to business-combination lock-up agreements.
redemption.rails: Bidirectional switching between forms is asserted in one subordinate clause: "holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ". Only the INBOUND leg is documented, and it is a coordination between two transfer agents rather than an internal book movement: the holder asks their broker to move the shares out of street name "through the Direct Registration System (DRS) or Deposit and Withdrawal at Custodian (DWAC) method" to Continental Stock Transfer (DRS & DWAC #7808); Continental then "records you as the registered owner of the shares" and issues a statement; and only "Once your shares are registered directly on the transfer agent's shareholder ledger" can they be converted into tokenized form and issued to a Securitize-registered wallet. Securitize warns that "Not all brokers support DRS transfers" and that broker fees vary. The OUTBOUND leg — de-tokenization back to the Continental book-entry position — has no published procedure, burn address, processing time or fee anywhere, and the unquantified switch latency is the constraint the S-1 itself blames for potential price discrepancies between the two forms.

transferRestrictions.mechanism: program-mediated, per-token whitelist. On-chain: Token-2022 DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified 2026-09-16), so every new SECZ token account is frozen at birth and only the freeze authority (8Twerer..., an apparent program PDA) can thaw it; plus PausableConfig for a global halt. Off-chain: the Securitize Connect API documents wallet whitelisting scoped to a specific token ('adds a wallet address to the whitelist of an specific token', requiring a tokenId, since 'in a given domain there may be multiple tokens'), with wallet statuses 'ready, pending, failed' and a 'not-authorised' response state. Notably the whitelist is NOT tied to a platform-hosted wallet: 'This is not required, as the whitelisting at token level does NOT require the wallet being registered at Securitize iD' — a self-custodied address can be whitelisted directly. Contractually: 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions', and specific Avalanche holdings carry business-combination lock-ups. US persons are the TARGET market here ('eligible U.S. investors'), which inverts the usual tokenized-equity geofence.

issuers.corporateActions: Securitize markets corporate-action servicing as a core transfer-agent capability — the S-1 describes 'a comprehensive suite of securities services including real-time approval, record-keeping, distributions, dividend issuances and compliance solutions' — so the institutional machinery genuinely exists and is exercised for third-party issuers (BUIDL and others). For SECZ specifically nothing has been exercised: Securitize Corp. declares no dividend, so the distribution path is untested on its own stock; the mint's ScaledUiAmount multiplier is 1, so no split has occurred; and no tokenized-holder proxy process or on-chain voting is documented. Two mechanisms are disclosed that are unusual and material. (1) FORK POLICY: 'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions. Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities' — a rare, explicit, pre-agreed chain-exception policy, and simultaneously a statement that the issuer, not the chain, decides. It adds that it 'would generally expect to follow the fork recognized by principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows' and that 'In extreme circumstances, Securitize may determine that migrating assets to an alternative fork is necessary'. (2) MANUAL FALLBACK: 'Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent' — an explicit off-chain recovery path that exists precisely because the chain is not the record. Emergency halt: PausableConfig on the mint, with no published policy for its use.

pricing.notes: The same class trades on NYSE under SECZ, so a continuous reference price exists, and the token has on-chain liquidity: 'Trading of Tokenized SECZ on Solana is now enabled via on-chain liquidity provision partners', and Jupiter priced the mint at ~$8.35 on 2026-09-16 with a reported holder count of 44 and roughly $1.24M market value. The issuer is candid about the basis risk in its own prospectus: 'the simultaneous existence of both could potentially fragment liquidity across platforms, affect bid-ask spreads (particularly outside NYSE trading hours), and result in price discrepancies between Tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ—especially if arbitrage is limited by operational or regulatory constraints', and 'Blockchain-based trading mechanisms may have significantly less liquidity and volume compared to national securities exchanges, such as NYSE'. Arbitrage is real but constrained twice over: the switch between forms has no published latency, and only broker-dealer-onboarded persons can hold the tokenized side at all, so the arbitrageur set is permissioned. Jupiter reported a -100% 24h volume change on 2026-09-16, i.e. no trades that day — the on-chain market exists but is thin. No oracle price feed for the Solana mint was located.

venues: On-chain liquidity on Solana via unnamed 'on-chain liquidity provision partners' (S-1). Jupiter indexes and prices the mint (isVerified true, tags token-2022/verified), so DEX routing exists — a materially more open venue posture than Bullish, where 'AMM and DEX trading are not yet enabled'.
Securitize's own SEC-registered broker-dealer and alternative trading system, 'approved for digital asset securities primary and secondary market trading'.
NYSE — for the non-tokenized common stock.
Avalanche — the larger tokenized deployment; venue arrangements there not examined.
Reported 2026-08-20 but unverified by rwa-sonar: SECZ linked to Solana on-chain credit markets (collateral use).

incidents.summary: Observation by rwa-sonar, not an announced incident: the widely-cited '$295 million of tokenized SECZ' does not correspond to the Solana deployment. The Solana Token-2022 mint held 148,998 tokens on 2026-09-16 (~$1.24M at ~$8.35), i.e. roughly 0.4% of the headline figure, across 117 token accounts. The S-1 places the locked-up business-combination shares on Avalanche, which is the likely home of the balance. The headline figure appears to be a cross-chain (or Avalanche-dominated) total that press coverage attached to the Solana launch; nothing published by the issuer breaks it down per chain. A grader reading '$295M on Solana' would be off by more than two orders of magnitude.

incidents.summary: Discrepancy inside the issuer's own prospectus, worth recording as the marketing-versus-instrument split this project exists to arbitrate. The S-1 business section says Securitize 'issues, manages, and records securities natively on-chain — meaning that instead of relying on disconnected systems across brokers, custodians, and clearinghouses, every transaction and ownership record is maintained on a single, verifiable ledger accessible in real time'. The same document's risk factors say multichain deployments 'are managed and reconciled through the same control book and master securityholder file', that in a fork 'Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record', and that Securitize keeps 'manual safeguards ... which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent'. The risk factors describe an off-chain control book with the chain as its projection; the business section describes the chain as the ledger. The risk factors are the operative description.

openQuestions: MINT ATTRIBUTION IS INFERRED, NOT PUBLISHED. Securitize has published no Solana contract address anywhere located. 5VzwKkvynPJzcgwhBe7ESEyNgqMbo15yBu7Sehssd9ED is attributed on the strength of its TokenMetadata URI pointing at metadata.securitize.io, matching name/symbol, the Token-2022 compliance extension set, a 2026-06-29 creation date (three days before listing) and a registry verified flag. That is strong circumstantial evidence, not issuer confirmation. Given four SECZ-branded impersonation mints on Solana, the single highest-value next step is asking Securitize IR to publish canonical addresses. Treat the address as high-confidence-but-unconfirmed until then.

Where is the $295M? Press reports $295M of tokenized SECZ; the Solana mint holds 148,998 tokens (~$1.24M). The S-1 puts locked-up business-combination shares on Avalanche, so the balance is presumably there — but Securitize publishes no per-chain supply figures and nothing reconciles the headline to the chains. The Avalanche contract address should be identified and its supply read to close this.

ANSWERED (2026-09-18): a tokenized holder is a registered holder in their own name, not a customer position behind the group's broker-dealer. Securitize's own tokenize instructions route the holder through direct registration BEFORE any token exists — the broker DRS/DWACs the shares to Continental Stock Transfer, "the transfer agent records you as the registered owner of the shares", the holder gets "an account statement or confirmation showing your name, account number, and the number of shares you hold", and only then can the position "be converted into tokenized form". Broker-dealer onboarding still gates ATS access and the whitelist still gates the wallet, but the ownership itself is direct registration. Residual gap: nothing published says whether the tokenized units are shown on Continental's ledger, on Securitize's control book, or on both.

What is the correct name of the gatekeeping broker-dealer? The S-1 says 'Securities Markets, LLC'; Securitize's broker-dealer is publicly known as Securitize Markets, LLC. Most likely a typo in a registration statement, but it is the entity that controls who may hold the security, and it should be confirmed against the FINRA/SEC BD registration rather than assumed.

Which entity holds the on-chain authorities, and under what program? 8Twerer... (mint + freeze) is an apparent PDA whose owning program was not identified; D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA... (permanent delegate, pause, split, metadata) was not resolved at all. Whether these sit with Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC (the regulated registrar) or with an operating affiliate matters legally, and whether the program has a timelock or multisig gate matters for grading. Fireblocks MPC is disclosed for corporate treasury only.

What are the 117 token accounts? 148,998 tokens across 117 accounts, with Jupiter reporting 44 holders and a top-holders concentration of ~11.7%. How many are investor self-custody wallets versus platform/custodian/liquidity-pool accounts is unknown. getTokenLargestAccounts on the public RPC returned HTTP 429 on 2026-09-16 and should be retried against a paid endpoint.

Who are the 'on-chain liquidity provision partners' on Solana? The S-1 says Solana trading 'is now enabled via on-chain liquidity provision partners' without naming them. Since holding SECZ requires whitelisting, a liquidity pool must itself be whitelisted — so the pool addresses, and whether pool LPs must be onboarded, are open. Jupiter reported zero volume in the 24h to 2026-09-16.

Is SECZ actually live as DeFi collateral? ANSWERED (2026-09-23): yes, on Loopscale. The second-largest SECZ token account, 6Nk983pK7GPa2FyVkj8crq3YQgbXZXA9wPipoBRY4Fhw (13,391.402983 SECZ at finalized slot 449676926), is owned by HUyo5aYaNQvodYmy8TmjnpcxQCk3PVsbyTJUyjmAihFx, a Loan account of program 1oopBoJG58DgkUVKkEzKgyG9dvRmpgeEm1AVjoHkF78 (Loan discriminator; DefiLlama's Loopscale adapter names that program as Loopscale). This matches Securitize's 2026-08-20 announcement that "Tokenized SECZ is now live within @Loopscale 's onchain credit markets on @solana" (as reproduced by The Crypto Times) for "Eligible holders". STILL OPEN: which price oracle values SECZ collateral and what a liquidation does when the liquidator's account is not on Securitize's allowlist (every new token account starts frozen), and whether the Loan account's token account was approved individually by Securitize. The protocols in the DeFi usage scan (Kamino, Jupiter Lend, Nest, Project 0, Save) do not include Loopscale, which is why this position was not in the scan.

Has the fork policy ever been applied, and who bears the loss? The S-1's fork provisions are the most developed chain-exception policy in this universe, but they allocate authority without allocating loss: nothing states what happens to a holder whose tokens end up on the chain Securitize does not recognise, or who compensates them. Also note the dependency it creates — the tie-break heuristic is whichever fork 'principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows' recognise.

How do dividends, proxy voting and splits work for a tokenized holder? Securitize sells 'distributions, dividend issuances' as transfer-agent services and runs them for third-party issuers, but Securitize Corp. pays no dividend, the ScaledUiAmount multiplier is 1, and no tokenized-holder proxy process is documented. Untested on its own stock. Note the earnout structure (VWAP thresholds of $15/$20/$25 triggering Securitize Earnout Shares over five years from Closing) will cause share issuance that must propagate to the mint — a live, dated test of the control-book-to-chain path.
What is the token-to-nontokenized switch latency and fee? Unpublished, and it is the constraint the S-1 itself blames for potential price discrepancies.

Has the Solana token program been independently audited? Nothing public ties an audit to this deployment, despite Securitize's scale (BUIDL alone was >60% of its tokenized AUM at 2025-09-30) and its 21-chain integration.

What is the de-tokenization route? The S-1 asserts holders "may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ" and the issuer publishes the inbound leg in full (DRS or DWAC to Continental, then issuance to a whitelisted wallet), but no document anywhere describes the outbound leg — no burn address, no request form, no latency, no fee and no statement of who bears the price risk while the position is in transit between the two forms.

How are the two registers reconciled, and which one governs? Continental Stock Transfer keeps the register of record for the common stock; Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC keeps the control book and master securityholder file for the tokenized units and is "the exclusive digital transfer agent". No transfer-agency agreement for SECZ is published on either side, so the division of the books, the reconciliation cadence and the tie-break on a discrepancy are all undisclosed — exactly the gap Bullish closes explicitly with its register-of-members tie-break.

RESOLVED 2026-09-17: the permanent-delegate/pause/split/metadata authority D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA1kEzKZNrdMvYKPLdZtrmAnnK6jCS is NOT a PDA - getAccountInfo returns an initialized, funded, system-program-owned account with zero data (499,971,639 lamports = 0.49997 SOL, owner 11111111111111111111111111111111, executable false), which is a plain keypair wallet with no multisig account behind it.
