blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: Securitize's own prospectus decides this three times over, against its own marketing. (1) The control book: multichain deployments 'are managed and reconciled through the same control book and master securityholder file to ensure that total outstanding units remain consistent and singular across chains' — a master securityholder file that reconciles the chains is by definition above them. (2) The fork policy: 'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions. Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities.' If the issuer picks which ledger is authoritative, the ledger is not authoritative. (3) The manual fallback: 'Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent.' Against this, the business section claims 'every transaction and ownership record is maintained on a single, verifiable ledger accessible in real time', and third-party commentary claims 'a transfer of a SECZ token on Solana or Avalanche constitutes a transfer of the underlying security in the official company records'. The latter may well describe the operational reality — the transfer agent and the chain operator are the same firm, so the propagation is immediate and there is no inter-party reconciliation gap, which is the strongest version of this architecture anyone is running. It is still a control book with an on-chain projection.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Gated at both layers. On-chain: the mint carries DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified 2026-09-16), so any account opened by a non-whitelisted wallet is frozen at birth and cannot receive; only the freeze authority (8Twerer...) can thaw it; and PausableConfig allows a global halt. Off-chain: whitelisting is per-token through the Securitize Connect API, and 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer.' The press release: 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions.' Specific Avalanche positions carry business-combination lock-ups on top. The one point in Securitize's favour: there IS on-chain liquidity ('trading ... enabled via on-chain liquidity provision partners', Jupiter-routable), so whitelisted-to-whitelisted trading including via pools actually works — better than Bullish, where AMM/DEX trading is disabled outright.

bearerRedemption.reason: Presenting the token to a third party gets you nothing. Switching between tokenized and nontokenized SECZ runs entirely through Securitize's own platform and requires broker-dealer onboarding: 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ', but only holders who 'meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC'. No burn address, no process, no timeframe and no fee is published. A holder outside the whitelist holds a token that is frozen at any new address and convertible nowhere.

forcedTransfers.reason: Verified on-chain 2026-09-16 and corroborated in the filing. The mint carries a PermanentDelegate (D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA1kEzKZNrdMvYKPLdZtrmAnnK6jCS) able to transfer or burn from any token account without the holder's signature, a freeze authority able to freeze any account, and PausableConfig able to halt every transfer at once. The S-1 describes the institutional counterpart: Securitize keeps 'manual safeguards ... which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent', and reserves the right in a fork to decide the authoritative record and even to migrate assets. So lost keys, theft, inheritance and court-ordered seizure are all addressable — the property that makes a registered-share tokenization legally usable and that no SPV tracker has.

titleDeed.reason: Stated in a registration statement, which is the strongest form this claim takes anywhere in the universe: 'we enabled Tokenized SECZ, a natively tokenized version of our common stock. Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class.' And: 'Tokenized SECZ provides an additional mechanism for investors to hold and transfer shares in the Company'; 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ'. The press release: 'issuer-sponsored tokenization of the same common stock trading on the NYSE'; 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share.' No SPV, receipt, derivative or tracker layer. Residual gap: no CUSIP/ISIN is published for the tokenized form and the token metadata carries none, so there is no identifier-level cross-check of the kind the Superstate peer provides.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Self-custody is supported at the mechanism level and this is documented rather than inferred: the Securitize Connect API states that whitelisting a wallet to a token 'does NOT require the wallet being registered at Securitize iD', so an arbitrary self-controlled address can be whitelisted directly to hold SECZ, and Securitize's own corporate holdings of Securitize-issued tokenized securities are described as 'held in self-custody utilizing Fireblocks infrastructure'. Caveats: (1) conditional — accounts are frozen at birth and only Securitize's whitelisting makes them usable, and it can re-freeze or pause; (2) the press release describes access as being 'through Securitize's regulated platform' and does not mention self-custody, so how many of the 117 token accounts are genuinely investor-controlled versus platform- or custodian-held is unknown.

issuerIndependent.reason: This is the weakest point in the structure and it is structural, not incidental. Securitize Corp. is simultaneously the securities issuer, the transfer agent, the tokenization platform, the broker-dealer and ATS that gate access, and the holder of the on-chain freeze, claw-back and pause authorities. There is no independent party anywhere — no independent recordkeeping transfer agent as in the Superstate peer, no third-party registrar as at Bullish today. If Securitize stops operating, no address can be thawed, no share can be tokenized or de-tokenized, the control book has no other keeper, and the 'manual safeguards' that back up the chain are its own. The SHARE would survive (Delaware common stock of a reporting company, and a successor transfer agent could be appointed); the TOKEN would not. Note the mitigant on key topology: the mint/freeze authority appears to be a program PDA rather than a plain wallet, which is better than Bullish's funded single key — but a program Securitize controls is still Securitize.

presetJurisdiction.reason: Unambiguous and documented in a registration statement: a Delaware corporation, US federal securities law, an SEC-registered transfer agent with a public file number (084-06638), an SEC-registered FINRA-member broker-dealer and ATS gating access, and an NYSE listing. The tokenized form is described in the issuer's own S-1 risk factors rather than only in press releases, which means the legal characterisation is made under Securities Act liability. This is the clearest 'yes' of the three issuers examined and the sharpest contrast with Bullish, which publishes no token instrument at all. The one soft spot is forward-looking rather than present: the S-1 itself notes 'market intermediaries may face unclear or evolving obligations' for tokenized securities.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Nothing independent is attached to the token and nothing independent is published about it. The mint's TokenMetadata additionalMetadata array is empty and its update authority is a Securitize-side address; the metadata URI carries name/symbol/description/image only. There is no attestation hook, no proof-of-reserve, no published reconciliation between mint supply and the master securityholder file, no smart-contract audit for the Solana deployment, and no public supply or holder API. The structural problem is worse here than elsewhere: with issuer, transfer agent, platform and broker-dealer all in one group, EVERY assertion about the register is first-party. Securitize's financial statements are audited and it is a reporting company, which is real but is not an attestation about the token.

aiReady.reason: KYC sits directly in the transfer loop, and here it is a broker-dealer's onboarding rather than a platform's: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer', with 'onboarding, KYC/AML verification, jurisdictional eligibility checks'. An autonomous agent cannot complete FINRA-member broker-dealer onboarding. Partial mitigation of the same kind the peer has: whitelisting is per-token and does not require a Securitize iD profile, and on-chain liquidity pools are live, so protocol addresses can evidently be whitelisted — but an agent still cannot get itself whitelisted. Fails on unconditionalTransfers regardless.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: Mechanism, obligation and institutional standing all present. Mechanically: PermanentDelegate, freeze authority and PausableConfig allow seizure, reversal, freezing and a market-wide halt without holder consent. Institutionally: the register is kept by an SEC-registered transfer agent (File No. 084-06638) subject to Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21, and the issuer is a reporting company, so lost-securityholder, escheat and regulatory-request obligations attach. Documented policy: the S-1's fork provisions commit the transfer agent to determine the authoritative record 'for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions', and the manual safeguards exist precisely so that ownership records survive on-chain failure. This is the most explicitly articulated chain-exception posture of the three issuers.

meetingOfMinds.reason: Buyer-and-seller agreement is not sufficient: both sides must be whitelisted to the specific token, and a counterparty must first pass a FINRA-member broker-dealer's onboarding. The press release is explicit that tokenization 'does not ... override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions', and specific Avalanche positions are subject to lock-ups that bind regardless of any agreement between the parties. A trade between two already-whitelisted wallets does settle without per-trade sign-off — and on Solana it can even settle through a liquidity pool, which is more than the Bullish peer allows — but the eligible counterparty set is determined by the issuer's own broker-dealer, and because there is no public allowlist a would-be buyer cannot verify their eligibility in advance.

findings.statement: Vertical integration is complete in the tokenization and trading layer and absent from the register of record. One group — Securitize Corp. — is the securities issuer, the platform that mints, the SEC-registered digital transfer agent that keeps the control book and master securityholder file for the tokenized units, the broker-dealer whose onboarding gates access, the ATS the tokens trade on, and the holder of the mint, freeze, permanent-delegate, pause and scaled-UI authorities. Every assertion about the TOKENIZED sub-register, the whitelist and the reconciliation between chains is therefore first-party, and the platform ToS state that "Securitize acts as agent of the relevant issuer, not as a fiduciary to investors". But the register of the common stock itself is kept by an independent third party: the S-1 and 424B3 Description of Securities name Continental Stock Transfer & Trust Company, and the issuer's own tokenize page gives its DRS & DWAC number.
findings.quote: The Transfer Agent for the Securitize Common Stock is Continental Stock Transfer & Trust Company.
findings.quoteNote: Downgraded from caution to info and narrowed on 2026-09-18. The earlier statement rested on "there is no independent transfer agent anywhere in the stack", which the S-1's own Description of Securities contradicts. What survives is the tokenization/ATS layer, where the integration is genuine and total; the finding is kept rather than deleted for that reason.

findings.statement: 'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights... Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities.' The tie-break heuristic is the fork recognised by the principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows, and Securitize reserves the right to migrate assets to another fork. Having a policy at all is rarer and better than not having one; the content allocates authority rather than loss, and is decisive evidence against the chain being the main ledger.

keyGovernance.evidence: RPC getAccountInfo, 2026-09-16 (stocks/findings.md, Securitize entry): the mint and freeze authority 8TwererfKZwiBfKQs2bQmVRrezqeFG3JvrVsbpGaPbQs returns null - zero lamports, never initialized - which is the shape of a PDA used as a CPI signer, so minting and thawing are program-mediated. The owning program was not identified and its upgrade authority is unknown. RESOLVED 2026-09-17: the permanent-delegate/pause/split/metadata authority D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA1kEzKZNrdMvYKPLdZtrmAnnK6jCS is NOT a PDA - getAccountInfo returns an initialized, funded, system-program-owned account with zero data (499,971,639 lamports = 0.49997 SOL, owner 11111111111111111111111111111111, executable false), which is a plain keypair wallet with no multisig account behind it. So claw-back, global pause and the split multiplier sit behind one ordinary private key even though minting and thawing are program-mediated. Which entity holds it is still unattributed. The rebase (scaledUiAmountConfig) authority is D2kGPFTyGSeeTSCA1kEzKZNrdMvYKPLdZtrmAnnK6jCS — the same address as the permanent delegate, pause and metadata authority — so it inherits that key's 'hot-key' characterisation. Multiplier 1, no pending change.

links.label: Ownership of the underlying

fields.value: The holder owns the actual registered common share. The S-1 risk factor is unambiguous on two points at once: 'we enabled Tokenized SECZ, a natively tokenized version of our common stock. Tokenized SECZ is not a separate share class' and 'Tokenized SECZ provides an additional mechanism for investors to hold and transfer shares in the Company'. The issuer's own press release adds that this is an 'issuer-sponsored tokenization of the same common stock trading on the NYSE' and that 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions.' Holders may move between forms: 'holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ'. There is no SPV, receipt or nominee layer in the legal structure — but access runs through a broker-dealer's onboarding, so whether the holder is a registered holder of record in their own name or a customer of the broker-dealer is NOT established by any document located, and this is the central unresolved question for this issuer.

No custodian is interposed for the security itself — the token is the share and the register is Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC's master securityholder file. For its own corporate digital assets Securitize discloses self-custody via Fireblocks MPC ('enables us to retain exclusive control over the authorization of transactions without ever generating or storing a traditional private key'), and states that 'In the case of Securitize-issued tokenized securities held in self-custody utilizing Fireblocks infrastructure, Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent.' Investor-side custody may be self-custody (see transferRestrictions) or broker/custodian-held; the split is not disclosed.

links.label: Issuance and redemption

fields.value: Holders who have completed the broker-dealer onboarding: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer.' The issuer's press release adds that the tokenized form is for 'eligible U.S. investors' subject to 'onboarding, KYC/AML verification, jurisdictional eligibility checks'. Certain Avalanche holdings are additionally subject to business-combination lock-up agreements.

Bidirectional switching between forms is asserted in one subordinate clause: "holders of SECZ may elect to switch between tokenized SECZ and nontokenized SECZ". Only the INBOUND leg is documented, and it is a coordination between two transfer agents rather than an internal book movement: the holder asks their broker to move the shares out of street name "through the Direct Registration System (DRS) or Deposit and Withdrawal at Custodian (DWAC) method" to Continental Stock Transfer (DRS & DWAC #7808); Continental then "records you as the registered owner of the shares" and issues a statement; and only "Once your shares are registered directly on the transfer agent's shareholder ledger" can they be converted into tokenized form and issued to a Securitize-registered wallet. Securitize warns that "Not all brokers support DRS transfers" and that broker fees vary. The OUTBOUND leg — de-tokenization back to the Continental book-entry position — has no published procedure, burn address, processing time or fee anywhere, and the unquantified switch latency is the constraint the S-1 itself blames for potential price discrepancies between the two forms.

links.label: Transfer and control

fields.value: program-mediated, per-token whitelist. On-chain: Token-2022 DefaultAccountState=Frozen (verified 2026-09-16), so every new SECZ token account is frozen at birth and only the freeze authority (8Twerer..., an apparent program PDA) can thaw it; plus PausableConfig for a global halt. Off-chain: the Securitize Connect API documents wallet whitelisting scoped to a specific token ('adds a wallet address to the whitelist of an specific token', requiring a tokenId, since 'in a given domain there may be multiple tokens'), with wallet statuses 'ready, pending, failed' and a 'not-authorised' response state. Notably the whitelist is NOT tied to a platform-hosted wallet: 'This is not required, as the whitelisting at token level does NOT require the wallet being registered at Securitize iD' — a self-custodied address can be whitelisted directly. Contractually: 'Tokenization changes the form of ownership; it does not change the underlying nature of the share or override applicable legal, contractual or transfer restrictions', and specific Avalanche holdings carry business-combination lock-ups. US persons are the TARGET market here ('eligible U.S. investors'), which inverts the usual tokenized-equity geofence.

links.label: Dividends and cash entitlements

fields.value: Securitize markets corporate-action servicing as a core transfer-agent capability — the S-1 describes 'a comprehensive suite of securities services including real-time approval, record-keeping, distributions, dividend issuances and compliance solutions' — so the institutional machinery genuinely exists and is exercised for third-party issuers (BUIDL and others). For SECZ specifically nothing has been exercised: Securitize Corp. declares no dividend, so the distribution path is untested on its own stock; the mint's ScaledUiAmount multiplier is 1, so no split has occurred; and no tokenized-holder proxy process or on-chain voting is documented. Two mechanisms are disclosed that are unusual and material. (1) FORK POLICY: 'In the event of such a fork, Securitize would determine which chain constitutes the valid and authoritative record for purposes of ownership, recordkeeping, and the exercise of holder rights such as voting, redemptions, and distributions. Tokens existing on other forked chains would not be recognized as valid representations of the securities' — a rare, explicit, pre-agreed chain-exception policy, and simultaneously a statement that the issuer, not the chain, decides. It adds that it 'would generally expect to follow the fork recognized by principal stablecoin issuers used in settlement flows' and that 'In extreme circumstances, Securitize may determine that migrating assets to an alternative fork is necessary'. (2) MANUAL FALLBACK: 'Securitize has manual safeguards in place which help retain the appropriate records of ownership should the automated blockchain systems fail which it controls in its capacity as transfer agent' — an explicit off-chain recovery path that exists precisely because the chain is not the record. Emergency halt: PausableConfig on the mint, with no published policy for its use.

fields.value: Two transfer agents, and only the tokenized one is an affiliate. (1) Continental Stock Transfer & Trust Company — SEC transfer agent File No. 084-00034, CIK 0000024179, DRS & DWAC #7808 — is the transfer agent of record for the Securitize common stock, named in the S-1/424B3 Description of Securities and in Securitize's own tokenize instructions, and independent of the issuer. (2) Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC — SEC transfer agent File No. 084-06638, CIK 0001782266 — is the "exclusive digital transfer agent for tokenized securities issued on Securitize's platform" and keeps the control book and master securityholder file for the tokenized units; it is an affiliate of the issuer, not an independent party, and is never named in the S-1. No transfer-agency agreement for SECZ is published on either side, so the division of the books between them, and how the two are reconciled, rests on the issuer's own description.

links.label: Regulatory permission and disclosure

fields.value: The most heavily regulated of the three Solana-native issuers examined, and the only one where the tokenization vendor is itself the registrant. The underlying security is registered common stock of a Delaware SEC-reporting company listed on the NYSE (S-4 registration statement effective 2026-06-05; S-1 filed 2026-07-31, EFFECT 2026-08-07; 424B3 prospectuses 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-13). Securitize Transfer Agent, LLC is an SEC-registered transfer agent (File No. 084-06638). The S-1 describes the group as 'the only vertically integrated tokenization provider with SEC-registered entities across a transfer agent, broker-dealer, alternative trading system (ATS), investor advisor and fund administration'. Access to the tokenized form is intermediated by a regulated broker-dealer: 'Access to Tokenized SECZ is restricted to holders who meet the onboarding requirements of Securities Markets, LLC, a SEC registered and FINRA member broker dealer' (note: the S-1 renders the entity name as 'Securities Markets, LLC'. RESOLVED 2026-09-17 against a primary source: Securitize's own 2026-07-02 press release names 'Securitize Markets, LLC, an SEC-registered broker-dealer and member FINRA/SIPC that operates an SEC-regulated Alternative Trading System (ATS)', so the S-1 wording is a typographical error in a registration statement and the gatekeeping broker-dealer is Securitize Markets, LLC). No exemptive relief or no-action letter for the tokenized form was located; the S-1 warns that 'market intermediaries may face unclear or evolving obligations'.

Delaware General Corporation Law governs the common stock and the share register; US federal securities law governs the listing, the transfer agent (Exchange Act §17A and Rules 17Ad-1 to 17Ad-21) and the broker-dealer/ATS gating access. No separate token terms of service or holder agreement for Tokenized SECZ was located; the operative public instrument is the Form S-1 prospectus risk factor plus the Securitize platform's general investor terms (not located in tokenized-SECZ-specific form).

issuers.issuingEntity: SHIFT DAO LLC, a for-profit series DAO limited liability company. Each product is a separate designated Series of that LLC (Series 12-18 observed) with its own executed Series Operating Agreement; the Company enters each agreement "solely in its limited and non-discretionary capacity as the administrative agent" and is "not a manager, managing member, fiduciary, or controlling person" of the Series. The initial nominee member of each Series is MINS LLC, Trust Company Complex, Ajeltake Road, Ajeltake Island, Majuro, MH 96960, which "holds its membership interest solely for purposes of facilitating the formation and annual renewal" and "has no economic entitlement or discretionary authority". The Series 17 agreement is digitally signed 2026-04-19 by Robin Van Niekerk on behalf of MINS LLC. No director, officer or operating-company entity is named; the team page lists twelve individuals with no roles and cites backgrounds at the Israel Securities Authority, Tel-Aviv Stock Exchange, Deloitte, Kraken, Flow Traders, Securitize, CheckPoint, Utila and Emurgo, and names SNZ Holding as seed-round lead investor. The entity that actually holds the backing ETFs is not named: the Solution Overview says only that "SHIFT engages with a private entity that holds the backing assets".
issuers.entityJurisdiction: Republic of the Marshall Islands. Formed under the Decentralized Autonomous Organization Act 2022 and governed under the Limited Liability Company Act 1996, with the Marshall Islands Business Corporations Act also cited in the Series agreements. Series segregation is asserted under LLC Act s.79. The Principal Office "need not be in the Marshall Islands" and the "Official Online Venue" for member participation is www.Shiftrwa.xyz.
issuers.governingLaw: Laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, stated in both the Terms of Use (s.12) and each Series Operating Agreement (Art. XII.2). Recourse is narrow: after a 30-day notice period a dispute "shall be settled by arbitration administered by the International Centre for Dispute Resolution", seated in the RMI, sole arbitrator, English, final and without appeal, and "No action at law or in equity based upon any claim arising out of or related to this Agreement shall be instituted in any court of any jurisdiction". The Terms of Use separately submit website disputes to "the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of RMI". Members owe and are owed no fiduciary duty (Art. IV.3, DAO Act s.109), and under Art. VI.2 (DAO Act s.111) "no one shall have the right under the LLC Act to demand to separately inspect or copy records" of the Series. A THIRD regime exists on the same issuer's vaults-only Terms, and it differs from both of the above: arbitration is "finally settled under the Rules of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce by one or more arbitrators appointed in accordance with the said Rules", with the seat "agreed by the parties" rather than fixed in the RMI, the same RMI governing law "without regard to its conflict of law principles", and - unlike the Series agreements - an express class waiver: "You agree that any disputes will be resolved on an individual basis, and you waive any right to participate in a class action lawsuit or class-wide arbitration." So one legal entity operates three inconsistent dispute regimes: ICDR with an RMI seat and a total court bar for a Series member, ICC with a negotiable seat and a class waiver for a vaults depositor, and the exclusive jurisdiction of the RMI courts for a website user. The Series agreements contain no class or consolidation provision at all, so collective redress there is unaddressed rather than waived - though sole-arbitrator bilateral arbitration reaches the same result.
issuers.regulatoryStatus: Unregistered and self-disclaiming, on top of a real company-law registration. The site-wide legal notice states the tokens "have not been registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933 ... or under the securities or financial-instrument laws of any other jurisdiction", that the issuer "is not registered or authorized as an investment company under the U.S. Investment Company Act of 1940 ... and is not authorized as an Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), an Undertaking for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS), or an investment firm under the laws of any EEA Member State", and that the tokens are "not offered, sold, or distributed in the United States or the United Kingdom, nor to any U.S. or U.K. persons or entities; in applicable jurisdictions they are offered only to 'qualified investors,' 'professional clients,' or their equivalent legal analogues". The Terms of Use add that the membership interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law, but purchasers are responsible for assessing their legal status in their jurisdiction". No prospectus, offering document or exemption filing was located in any jurisdiction, and no licence for the Series tokens - but a licence CLAIM does exist, on a different product's page. The vaults-only Terms state: "Shift DAO LLC is a corporate entity in RMI with an international investment business license and registration number 10246-26.", with a Majuro registered address (PO Box 852, Long Island Rd) and physical address (852 Lagoon Rd). Three things qualify it. (1) SCOPE: that page governs Shift Vaults - stablecoin staking and secured lending to a Cayman SPC - not the leveraged Series tokens in this dossier, and no licence claim appears in any Series Operating Agreement, in the Terms of Use, in the Risk Disclosure or in the site-wide legal notice, all of which instead deny registered or authorised status. (2) VERIFICATION: the number could not be checked against any Marshall Islands register - no public searchable register of RMI international investment business licences was located - so it is recorded as unverified, not as false. (3) CONSISTENCY: an investment-business licence, if real, would sit oddly beside the same issuer's statement that the interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law".
issuers.holderClaim: On paper: a membership interest in a designated Series of SHIFT DAO LLC whose sole purpose is to "acquire, hold, and maintain in its treasury assets whose economic performance corresponds to" one named index or stock. The Series 17 agreement says "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and Art. IV.1 says "Series Members are granted treasury ownership only", with no voting, management or fiduciary rights. In practice three things break that chain. (1) The issuer's own site-wide legal notice says the opposite: "The Series tokens provide their holders with economic exposure to the value of the Series Assets; holding the Tokens does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets." (2) The executed Series agreements do not identify the token they govern - membership is obtained by holding a token "created from and constricted by the parameters defined in the Smart Contract located at an address and a blockchain to be determined" - so no published document links the SPL mint that trades on Jupiter to the Series whose treasury holds the asset; the Series 17 (S&P 500) agreement compounds this by requiring "at least one (1) TSLA Short SHFT Token". (3) What the Series is documented to hold is not the referenced equity but a daily-reset leveraged ETF share (Series 17: SPXL, Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3x, ISIN US25459W8626; Series 12: Direxion Daily TSLA X2, ISIN US25460G2865), so exposure to Tesla or the S&P 500 is delivered through a third party's derivative fund. Graded as derivative for that reason; if the Series agreements' "owners in the Series Assets" language controlled and were bound to these mints, the record would move to spv-claim-redeemable.
issuers.underlyingCustodian: Two custodians are named, in the Risk Disclosure only: "Each Series relies on DekaBank, a European regulated financial institution, and ALPACADB LTD, a U.S.-regulated broker, as custodians of the Series Assets." The Collateral & Custody page adds that backing is held "with FINRA-registered, SEC-regulated brokerage partners" in "dedicated accounts, separate from operational balances and from other clients' assets" and "off-balance-sheet". Marketing and press name Alpaca Markets as the brokerage rail. The holding entity itself is not named ("a private entity that holds the backing assets"), nor is the market maker that operates the B2B mint/burn endpoints, and no account, statement, holdings report or balance for any Series has been published.

custodyVerification.agent: Chainlink Proof-of-Reserves is claimed as the verification agent and no such feed exists. Re-verified directly on 2026-09-18: Chainlink's own reference-data directory carries no SHIFT feed on either network (295 Ethereum-mainnet feeds, 12 Solana-mainnet feeds; the single "shift" string match is Coinshift's USPC NAV feed), no contract and no report was located, and the integration has been forthcoming since 2025-05-21
custodyVerification.frequency: claimed continuous - "The feed publishes the verified reserve state on-chain, every block" - but nothing observed at any cadence
custodyVerification.notes: Claimed, not evidenced. The docs assert Chainlink PoR "runs continuously, verifying that every Series Token in circulation is backed 1:1" and that "the SHIFT smart contract cannot issue tokens in excess of verified reserves; mint operations are gated by PoR feed". Verified 2026-09-16 and re-verified 2026-09-17: the PoR dashboard link on that same page still reads "[TO BE UPDATED]" and the third-party attestation section still reads "[TO BE UPDATED]", and no Chainlink PoR feed naming SHIFT could be found. The app dashboard link has changed: on 2026-09-16 the page pointed to https://app.shiftrwa.xyz, which redirected to /coming-soon; on 2026-09-17 the page points to shift-rwa.vercel.app/app, and both https://shift-rwa.vercel.app/app and https://app.shiftrwa.xyz/ return HTTP 200 client-rendered pages. Neither publishes a reserve figure: the Vercel app renders "TSL2L $0.00" and "TSL1S $0.00" under Top Movers, and app.shiftrwa.xyz returns an empty SPA shell. The earlier marketing site states PoR is "coming with mainnet". The on-chain record contradicts the gating claim outright: every observed issuance is a bare SPL Token-2022 mintTo signed by the mint's own authority keypair plus a fee payer, with no SHIFT program, oracle account or PoR account in the transaction at all. RE-VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY 2026-09-18, and this is now a negative finding rather than an unlocated one: Chainlink's reference-data directory was read directly - reference-data-directory.vercel.app/feeds-mainnet.json (295 feeds) and /feeds-solana-mainnet.json (12 feeds) - and contains no SHIFT feed on either network; the only entry matching the string "shift" is Coinshift's "USPC NAV". The promise is dated: a 2025-05-21 report of SHIFT joining the Chainlink BUILD programme says "To increase user trust, SHIFT will integrate Chainlink's Proof of Reserve for its tokenized assets", i.e. sixteen months of "will". So the gating claim - "the SHIFT smart contract cannot issue tokens in excess of verified reserves; mint operations are gated by PoR feed" - has no feed to gate on, in addition to having no program in any observed mint transaction.

securityInterest.holder: none - no charge, pledge, lien or security agent is created; the Series is documented as owning its treasury outright under LLC Act s.79 segregation

redemption.eligibility: Contradicted between primary documents. Each Series Operating Agreement grants a member a redemption right: "If a Member wishes to transfer their token back to the Series in exchange for funds, this is an internal membership-interest repurchase ... This transaction is available only to Members processed by smart contract where the transaction is settled directly from the treasury to the Member's wallet, not using any third-party assets." The Technical Overview says the opposite: "End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly. Mint and burn are B2B endpoints used by professional market makers to maintain inventory. Users acquire Series Tokens by swapping on Jupiter against market-maker liquidity." U.S. and U.K. persons are excluded from membership entirely.
redemption.rails: Documented retail path: internal membership-interest repurchase settled from the Series treasury by smart contract. Documented operational path: market makers mint and burn against the underlying ETF through B2B endpoints, 24/5 in line with U.S. trading hours, while user-facing trading is 24/7 RFQ on Jupiter, Meteora, Kamino and Orca. No burn address, latency, SLA or minimum is published for either path, and no SHIFT program exists on-chain to implement the smart-contract repurchase.
redemption.fees: Primary market: "The per-token purchase price shall equal the executed market price paid in a bona fide transaction to acquire one (1) share of [the named ETF], plus a transaction fee equal to 0.1% of such executed price." Ongoing: "The Master DAO is allowed to charge operational fees to the Series using a percentage-of-treasury formula" - the percentage is never stated in the master or any Series agreement. Secondary market: "User-facing trading costs are reflected in the RFQ spread quoted by market makers", tightest in U.S. hours and widest at weekends; the two docs pages give different weekend ceilings ("up to ~3%" in Solution Overview, "up to ~5%" in Risk Management). No transfer fee is charged on-chain: none of the eight mints carries a transferFeeConfig extension.

issuers.corporateActions: Nothing is passed through and nothing is applied by Shift. "Membership interests represent a limited economic interest in the Assets of the Series 17 treasury and do not provide any expectation of profit, income, or dividends." Leverage resets are the ETF issuer's: "SHIFT does not perform rebalancing. The leverage is delivered by the underlying ETF (e.g., Direxion TSLL), which manages its own daily reset internally. SHIFT simply tokenizes the ETF position 1:1. Nothing happens at 4 PM ET inside the SHIFT protocol." Wind-down is issuer-decided: on a "Master Cancellation Event" the Master DAO alone determines, in its administrative capacity, whether each Series "(i) continue[s] as an independent DAO LLC" or "(ii) be dissolved and wound up", and "all applicable fees, costs, and third-party expenses associated with such continuation shall be borne by the applicable Series or its members". Membership can also end involuntarily - "the person's involuntary immediate automatic withdrawal of their status as a Member, if the person is deemed a Restricted Person" - and Art. VII.2 provides that voluntary or involuntary cessation "does not give rise to any right of a Member to a distribution of any property or economic resources". Separately, the scaledUiAmountConfig authority on every mint lets the issuer restate all displayed balances; SOX3S already sits at multiplier 0.1.

pricing.notes: The issuer publishes no NAV, mark or indicative value for any Series Token at any cadence, and no oracle carries a price for them (rwa-sonar's own reference-price probe returns refSource null for all 8: "leveraged; no 1:1 reference"; the Shift symbols also truncate their underlyings, TSL2L to TSL and SOX3L to SOX, so no ticker join is possible). The user-facing price is a market maker's RFQ quote "based on the underlying ETF's NAV, plus a spread", and the spread is neither published nor bounded in any document. The primary-market price is anchored to a real exchange print - the executed price of one share of the named Direxion ETF plus 0.1% - so arbitrage against a public NAV is structurally possible, but only for the authorized market makers who can reach the mint/burn endpoints, and only 24/5. Observed secondary market on 2026-09-16: Jupiter reports null DEX liquidity on all eight mints, USD 117.91 of total 24h volume across all of them, organicScore 0 on every one, and a first pool for only 3 of 8 (all created 2026-07-31).

openQuestions: Which document controls? The executed Series agreements say "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and grant "treasury ownership only", while the site-wide legal notice says holding the tokens gives no "legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets". The whole claim-depth grade turns on this and the issuer publishes both.

Which mint does each Series Operating Agreement actually govern? Every agreement locates the token in "the Smart Contract located at an address and a blockchain to be determined", and the Series 17 (S&P 500) agreement requires "at least one (1) TSLA Short SHFT Token". Nothing published links the mints that trade to the Series that hold the assets.

What backs SPCX2L and SPCX2S, and under what Series? Both mints are live and trading, neither appears in the docs' Series or contract-address tables, and no Operating Agreement exists. Direxion's 2x SpaceX bull ETF (LOFF) listed on NYSE Arca on 15 June per Structured Retail Products, and a bear counterpart (LOFD) was announced later - was either instrument held when 250 SPCX2L were minted on 2026-06-16 and 395.72 SPCX2S on 2026-06-24?

ANSWERED (2026-09-18): no. The Chainlink Proof-of-Reserves integration that the docs describe as gating every mint and publishing every block does not exist. Chainlink's own reference-data directory was read end to end on both networks - 295 Ethereum-mainnet feeds and 12 Solana-mainnet feeds - and contains no SHIFT feed; the only entry matching "shift" is Coinshift's USPC NAV. The dashboard link is still "[TO BE UPDATED]", no observed mint transaction touches an oracle or reserve account, and the integration has been announced as forthcoming since 2025-05-21, when SHIFT joined the Chainlink BUILD programme ("SHIFT will integrate Chainlink's Proof of Reserve for its tokenized assets"). Recorded in findings as no-reserve-verification-published, severity critical. What remains open is only whether it is still intended: Chainlink Labs has said it is concluding BUILD-programme arrangements.

Is there any SHIFT Solana program? The docs describe "the SHIFT Solana program" that "mints, burns, and tracks Series Token supply" and audited "open-source" contracts, but every observed issuance is a raw Token-2022 mintTo signed by a bare keypair.

PARTLY ANSWERED (2026-09-18), and the answer is circumstantial rather than documentary. ARTokens GmbH is "an Austrian token issuer" registered at Simmeringer Hauptstrasse 24, Vienna, issuing asset-referenced tokens under MiCAR, whose own site advertises exactly Shift's pitch: "Backing asset reserves are verified via Chainlink Proof of Reserve and periodic audits". Four of the employer names on Shift's anonymous team page turn up as roles on ARTokens' named one - a "Flow Traders former CTO" as CTO, a "Securitize former Software Engineer and Architect" who is also "ex- CheckPoint", and an "ex-Utila" VP R&D. And the 2025-05-21 Chainlink BUILD report describes SHIFT itself as "building Asset-Referenced Tokens (ARTokens) - MiCAR-compliant digital assets backed by stocks, bonds, and ETFs". Suggestive of a shared team or a shared lineage; NOT proof of affiliation, and no corporate link is disclosed on either side. It still does not make a Zokyo review of ARTokens' Ethereum ERC-20 "aRtoken.sol" an audit of these eight Solana mints, which is what Shift's Audits page uses it for.
Why is SOX3S on a scaled-UI multiplier of 0.1 when the other seven mints are on 1? No document mentions the multiplier.
What is the Master DAO's percentage-of-treasury fee? Both the master and the Series agreements authorise it and neither states a number.

Which restriction list binds? There are now FOUR, from one issuer, and they do not agree. (1) The executed Series agreements - the only documents a Series member is actually party to - define Restricted Persons as UN-listed persons plus residents of Iran, Syria, Cuba, North Korea and Crimea/Donetsk/Luhansk, and do NOT exclude U.S. or U.K. persons. (2) The Terms of Use, Risk Disclosure and site notice exclude U.S. and U.K. persons explicitly and threaten "immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation". (3) The vaults-only Terms add OFAC and any "list of prohibited or restricted parties", exclude the United States by name, and name 24 jurisdictions. (4) The vaults KYC/AML page repeats those 24 and then extends to the whole FATF blacklist and greylist - "jurisdictions identified by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) as High-Risk Jurisdictions subject to a Call for Action or Jurisdictions under Increased Monitoring" - and says screening is enforced pre-block by the sequencer. Lists (3) and (4) are written for the vaults product, so a Series holder cannot tell whether they apply; the binding agreement remains the narrowest of the four.

Where did "over $40M in liquidity" go? Press reporting from the June 2026 Jupiter listing cites that figure; on 2026-09-16 Jupiter reports no DEX liquidity on any Shift mint, USD 3.26M of combined market cap and USD 117.91 of 24h volume.

Is the leveraged programme still being invested in, or is it being succeeded? www.shiftrwa.xyz now leads with covered-call vaults on SPY and COPX while /faq, /markets, /blog, /status and the Operating Agreement PDFs 404 on that domain and survive only on a Vercel preview host.
Who is the market maker with mint and burn access, and who is the "private entity that holds the backing assets"? Neither is named, and both sit between the holder and the ETF.

Does the RMI "international investment business license and registration number 10246-26" claimed on the vaults Legal & Compliance page exist, and would it cover the Series tokens? The number appears nowhere else - not in any Series Operating Agreement, the Master agreement, the Terms of Use, the Risk Disclosure or the site-wide legal notice, all of which deny authorised status - and no public searchable Marshall Islands register of such licences was located, so it is recorded as unverified. It also sits oddly beside the same issuer's position that the interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law".

Do the vaults-only legal pages bind a Series holder at all? Four documents that a holder would reasonably read as Shift's legal terms - Legal & Compliance, KYC/AML, Bankruptcy Remote Structure and the vaults FAQ - are written for Shift Vaults (stablecoin staking and secured lending to OpenTrade SPC, a Cayman SPC with an independent board and an FCA-regulated operator). They carry a different arbitration forum, a class-action waiver, wider restriction lists, an OFAC screening regime, freeze-and-seize smart-contract powers and a bankruptcy-remote structure that the Series tokens do not have. Nothing on the legal hub tells a Series holder which pages govern them.

keyGovernance.evidence: Verified 2026-09-16 by RPC. Each mint has its own single authority address that simultaneously holds mintAuthority, freezeAuthority, permanentDelegate, metadataUpdateAuthority, pause and scaled-UI authority (SPX3L CoghvrToe8SZTta5Q6cb2BnVki6WXXGMogeSiea5vNte; SPX3S 2CeU1GEWbhXXZvypMfAPa2AzyvF3yhrG7AqUyFoDqxZf; TSL2L 21bymdv3CB8QFa5taouuTcrgTVLjH9vKVEScEKqKGRZd; TSL1S 9eo5QkvdxsAU6kdAbAABWpbq1TGvsxPkLoroPwgxY4o1; SOX3L 2g5JvVx2C6si9XoLoMjr1CEyK8Mt597qptsrNN1RZ4WB; SOX3S 76ThePy3xFjiAvEn2dxymehQJBGoD2vywfYVNgXGVJVA; SPCX2L ELt7GJcL4jxVoF1snNjxjegPKjuELxi13ut5f8R7vgH; SPCX2S 4mU3jH1iEA78LJ9YPfFYnN4ABty6xMBxndajFg3iToaK). getMultipleAccounts returns null for all eight, i.e. they are unfunded, dataless addresses, and each one nevertheless appears as a true transaction signer on raw Token-2022 mintTo instructions with a separate funded fee payer (2HfsYtL44s9FXVjit21VUfvW4fP6FvvqHHWNan6puTWz) - so they are plain off-chain Ed25519 keypairs, not program-derived addresses (a PDA cannot sign at the transaction level) and not Squads or any other multisig (no multisig program appears in any of the transactions). Recorded as hot-key with that nuance: single-key control, fees sponsored by another wallet. The mints themselves were created on 2026-05-12 to 2026-06-11 by HJfhNwwaDqcUc7k5J8N5y3y1xHZ7qDYMsC7YFpp9fCdp with a plain createAccount + initialize* + setAuthority script. No threshold, timelock or governance process is disclosed for any of these keys, and none of the eight addresses appears in any Shift document. The rebase (scaledUiAmountConfig) authority is the same per-mint key that already holds mint, freeze, pause, metadata and permanent delegate — eight distinct keys, one per mint — so it inherits their 'hot-key' characterisation. The mechanism is in use, not merely armed: SOX3S (authority 76ThePy3xFjiAvEn2dxymehQJBGoD2vywfYVNgXGVJVA) reads a multiplier of 0.1, so a displayed SOX3S balance is already one tenth of its raw amount.

blockchainIsMainLedger.reason: Membership is defined by token holding: "A person becomes a Member by obtaining at least one (1) [Series] SHFT Token", and each holder "shall be deemed to have agreed to and be bound by this Agreement upon such person's acquiring" it. The Series records required by Art. VI.1 are "the name of each current and former Member or the unique Distributed Ledger identifier(s) attributable to each Member", and where the activity is on a distributed ledger with public human-readable explanations "there shall be no separate requirement to keep books of accounts". No transfer agent, share register or off-chain holder list exists anywhere in the documents. The caveat that keeps this from being clean: the agreements never name the mint, locating the token smart contract at "an address and a blockchain to be determined", so the chain is the register of a Series whose own agreement does not identify which chain or which mint.

unconditionalTransfers.reason: Nothing gates a transfer today, on any of the eight mints: defaultAccountState is initialized (new accounts are not frozen), the transferHook slot is initialized with a null programId, there is no allowlist, and there is no transferFeeConfig at all. Any wallet can send to any wallet, and the tokens are marketed as "24/7 permissionless" and composable on Jupiter, Meteora, Kamino and Orca. Control is entirely reactive: the permanentDelegate, freeze and pause powers are exercised after the fact, and the Risk Disclosure says a U.S. or U.K. person who bypasses the restrictions "may result in immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation of the associated tokens without recourse".

bearerRedemption.reason: Presenting the token compels delivery from nobody. The Series Operating Agreement's repurchase right is to be "processed by smart contract", and no SHIFT program exists on-chain to process it - every observed issuance is a raw Token-2022 mintTo by a keypair. The Technical Overview states plainly that "End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly" and that mint and burn are "B2B endpoints used by professional market makers", the app that would front a redemption resolves to /coming-soon, backing operations run only 24/5, and U.S. and U.K. persons are barred from membership entirely. Observed burns are negligible: on SOX3L the sum of all mintTo amounts (3,967.41007219) exceeds current supply (3,967.37399156) by 0.03608063 tokens, i.e. about 0.0009% of supply has ever been retired.

forcedTransfers.reason: Confirmed in both law and code. All eight mints carry a live permanentDelegate plus freezeAuthority and pausableConfig, all three held by the same single key per mint. The Risk Disclosure authorises the use: any attempt by a U.S. or U.K. person to bypass the restrictions "including the use of VPNs or proxy entities - is a material breach of the Operational Agreement and may result in immediate freezing, confiscation, or forced liquidation of the associated tokens without recourse", and Art. VII of each Series agreement makes Restricted-Person status trigger "involuntary immediate automatic withdrawal" of membership with no right to a distribution.

titleDeed.reason: The site-wide legal notice is explicit: holding the tokens "does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets", and each Series "is not affiliated with, sponsored by, or endorsed by" the trademark owners it references. Even on the Series agreements' more generous reading ("treasury ownership only"), the treasury asset is a Direxion daily-reset leveraged ETF share, not the referenced equity, so the token is at best a derived interest two layers away from Tesla or the S&P 500.

tokenSelfCustody.reason: Ordinary Token-2022 mints, held in any Solana wallet: "Holders custody the token in any Solana wallet. There is no liquidation engine and no forced close", and "SPL tokens held in any Solana wallet. No exchange custody." No KYC or allowlist gates holding, and Phantom, OKX Wallet and other wallets are listed integrations.

issuerIndependent.reason: The token cannot outlive its administrator on its own terms. On a "Master Cancellation Event" the Master DAO alone decides whether each Series continues as an independent DAO LLC or is wound up, and the members pay for continuation. The documented value chain runs entirely through parties the holder cannot reach: an unnamed "private entity that holds the backing assets", unnamed market makers who alone can mint and burn, and an administrator that owes no fiduciary duty and is subject to no court action in any jurisdiction. Nothing independent of Shift attests the reserve, and no NAV or PoR feed exists to price the token if Shift stopped publishing.

presetJurisdiction.reason: Unusually well pinned down for this cohort. A named issuer (SHIFT DAO LLC), a named jurisdiction (Republic of the Marshall Islands, DAO Act 2022 and LLC Act 1996), a stated governing law (RMI, in both the Terms of Use and every Series agreement), a named nominee member with a Majuro address (MINS LLC, Trust Company Complex, Ajeltake Road) and a fixed forum (ICDR arbitration seated in the RMI). The flag asks whether the jurisdiction is preset, and it is; what the jurisdiction is worth is another matter, since the agreements bar any court action anywhere and remove both fiduciary duties and inspection rights.

thirdPartyAttestations.reason: Every third-party verification Shift claims is either absent or somebody else's. Chainlink Proof-of-Reserves is described as running "continuously" and publishing "every block" and as gating mints, yet the PoR dashboard link reads "[TO BE UPDATED]", no Chainlink PoR feed naming SHIFT could be located, and the observed mints carry no oracle account at all. The "Third-party attestation" heading in the Collateral & Custody page is an empty "[TO BE UPDATED]". The sole file on the Audits page is a Zokyo review of ARTokens GmbH's Ethereum ERC-20 contract dated 19 June 2025. No custodian confirmation, holdings statement or reconciliation output has ever been published by DekaBank, ALPACADB LTD or anyone else.

aiReady.reason: Follows the definition: unconditionalTransfers is yes and tokenSelfCustody is yes, so an agent can hold and trade these tokens with no KYC and no allowlist. Three caveats that the flag does not capture: an agent cannot truthfully make the non-U.S./non-U.K.-person representation membership requires, it holds an asset subject to clawback, freeze and global pause by a single key, and there is effectively no market to trade into - USD 117.91 of 24h volume across all eight mints and no reported DEX liquidity on any of them.

reflectLegalDecisions.reason: The mechanism exists but no document binds it to a legal process. The clawback, freeze and pause powers are triggered by the issuer's own determination - Restricted-Person status or "a material breach of the Operational Agreement" such as VPN use - not by a court or regulator, and no procedure, notice period or appeal is published. The Restricted-Person definition does track external legal instruments (the UN Security Council Consolidated List and OFAC-embargoed regions), which is the one point in Shift's favour, but the same agreements bar any court action "in any court of any jurisdiction" and remove inspection rights, so there is no ordinary forum in which a holder-facing order could be obtained and then reflected on-chain.

meetingOfMinds.reason: A DEX or peer-to-peer transfer settles on the agreement of buyer and seller alone: no issuer signature, allowlist check, transfer hook or KYC step sits in the transfer path on any of the eight mints. Validity can be undone afterwards by clawback or freeze, but the transfer itself needs no third party.

The Series agreements add "Series Members are granted treasury ownership only. Members shall have no voting rights, management rights, or authority to participate in the control or operation of the Series", and the FAQ: "A Series membership grants you an exclusive economic interest in the assets held by the Series treasury, but it does not include voting or management rights."

attestations.statement: Risk Disclosure: "Each Series relies on DekaBank, a European regulated financial institution, and ALPACADB LTD, a U.S.-regulated broker, as custodians of the Series Assets", held in "dedicated accounts, separate from operational balances and from other clients' assets" with "FINRA-registered, SEC-regulated brokerage partners". Recorded unknown: neither named firm has published any confirmation, account statement or holdings report tied to these Series, the entity that actually holds the ETFs is described only as "a private entity", and no Series is identified in any custodian document.

attestations.statement: Series 17 Operating Agreement: "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and Art. IV.1 "Series Members are granted treasury ownership only", each Series "acting functionally as its own LLC with distinct assets, liabilities, and objectives" under LLC Act s.79. Recorded unknown because the issuer's own site-wide notice denies exactly this ("does not grant ... legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets") and because the agreement does not identify the mint it governs ("an address and a blockchain to be determined"), so the traded SPL token cannot be shown to be the membership interest described.

findings.quote: → Proof-of-Reserves dashboard [TO BE UPDATED]
findings.statement: 1:1 backing is the central product claim, nothing verifies it, and the verifier named is absent from the verifier's own directory. Chainlink PoR is said to run "continuously", to publish "the verified reserve state on-chain, every block" and to gate minting - "the SHIFT smart contract cannot issue tokens in excess of verified reserves; mint operations are gated by PoR feed". Measured against that: the PoR dashboard link on that page is "[TO BE UPDATED]", the "Third-party attestation" section is "[TO BE UPDATED]", Chainlink's reference-data directory carries no SHIFT feed on Ethereum mainnet (295 feeds) or Solana mainnet (12 feeds) when read directly on 2026-09-18, every observed issuance is a bare Token-2022 mintTo with no oracle or reserve account in the transaction, and no custodian statement or holdings report has ever been published. The integration was announced as forthcoming on 2025-05-21 with SHIFT's entry to the Chainlink BUILD programme and has not shipped in the sixteen months since.
findings.quoteNote: Strengthened 2026-09-18 without changing severity (already critical). The earlier statement said "no Chainlink feed naming SHIFT could be located", which read as a search limitation. Chainlink's own reference-data directory has now been read end to end on both networks and the feed is positively absent, and the promise has been dated to 2025-05-21.

findings.statement: All eight mints carry pausableConfig with a live authority (paused=false on 2026-09-16), so one key per product can halt every transfer of that token at once, with no court, regulator or notice period involved. The product is marketed as "24/7 permissionless".

findings.quote: scaledUiAmountConfig: {authority: 76ThePy3xFjiAvEn2dxymehQJBGoD2vywfYVNgXGVJVA, multiplier: 0.1} on SOX3S; multiplier: 1 on the other seven mints
findings.statement: Every Shift mint carries scaledUiAmountConfig under the same single authority, so all displayed balances can be restated by changing one multiplier. This is not hypothetical: SOX3S already sits at multiplier 0.1 while the other seven are at 1, and no Shift document mentions the multiplier, explains the SOX3S value or commits to a notice period for changing it.

findings.quote: mintTo: {amount: 39571858898, mint: FtBpBcLU4Epjm2nnuQNRYGkFM6jfsXrcGKJSiKCtSHFT, mintAuthority: 4mU3jH1iEA78LJ9YPfFYnN4ABty6xMBxndajFg3iToaK}; instructions: ComputeBudget, AToken createIdempotent, Token-2022 mintTo (no program, oracle or reserve account)
findings.statement: Issuance is unconditioned. 395.71858898 SPCX2S were minted on 2026-06-24 while the issuer's own markets page carried SPCX2S as not yet tradable and a June 2026 report said its launch was "subject to the availability of the underlying market instrument"; no Series Operating Agreement for a SpaceX Series has ever been published. findings.quote: Each Series of SHIFT DAO LLC operates under its own dedicated Operating Agreement, issued under the Marshall Islands DAO LLC Act. Final executed copies are linked below; additional Series are posted here as they go live.
findings.statement: Two of the eight live mints have no terms at all. The operating-agreements page publishes the master agreement plus Series 12, 13, 14, 15, 17 and 18; SPCX2L and SPCX2S are covered by no agreement, appear in neither the Product Overview Series table nor the Contract addresses table, and therefore have no documented Series, no defined permitted Assets, no price formula and no redemption right - while trading on Jupiter under the Shift name and tag.

findings.quote: WHEREAS, Series 17 is designated solely to acquire, hold, and maintain in its treasury assets whose economic performance corresponds to the S&P 500® index (the “Assets”), as established and approved by the Master DAO.
findings.statement: The Series agreements define the treasury contents openly: Series 17 is "designated solely to acquire, hold, and maintain in its treasury assets whose economic performance corresponds to the S&P 500 index (the 'Assets'), as established and approved by the Master DAO", and "The Master DAO shall define via its own governance process, which asset the Series acquires and holds". A specific ETF (SPXL, ISIN US25459W8626) is named only in the pricing formula, not as a binding holdings constraint, so the Series is not contractually confined to the instrument the marketing names.

findings.quote: End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly. Mint and burn are B2B endpoints used by professional market makers to maintain inventory.
findings.statement: The Series agreements grant a member redemption "processed by smart contract ... settled directly from the treasury to the Member's wallet", while the Technical Overview says "End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly" and mint/burn are "B2B endpoints used by professional market makers". No SHIFT program exists on-chain to process a member repurchase, the app front-end is at /coming-soon, and observed net burns are negligible (SOX3L: total minted 3,967.41007219 versus supply 3,967.37399156, a net 0.03608063 tokens retired).

findings.quote: Weekends Widest (up to ~3%) No primary-market access for two days; inventory cannot be replenished or hedged
findings.statement: The docs acknowledge the gap - "Backing operations (ETF purchases) run 24/5, in line with U.S. trading hours. User-facing trading on Jupiter remains 24/7" - but state no latency, SLA or bound for mint, burn or redemption, and the two pages disagree on the resulting cost: weekend spreads "Widest (up to ~3%)" in Solution Overview against "up to ~5%" in Risk Management.

findings.quote: Shift — trade tokenized stocks and ETFs with built-in 2x and 3x leverage, long or short, on-chain. No forced liquidations.
findings.statement: Shift publishes no NAV, indicative value or valuation output for any Series Token at any cadence. The markets page shows "Loading live price..." and "On-chain TVL feed wires up next, with the indexer", the app dashboard is /coming-soon, and the only price a holder can see is a market maker's RFQ quote whose spread is neither published nor bounded.

findings.quote: 67 tickers match no Pyth feed (BRK.B, many ETFs, Shift-truncated SOX/TSL/SPX).
findings.statement: No oracle publisher carries a price for any Shift mint. The Shift symbols truncate their underlyings (TSL2L to TSL, SOX3L to SOX, SPX3L to SPX), so no Pyth equity feed matches, and the repo's own probe resolves all eight to refSource null with the note "leveraged; no 1:1 reference" (stocks/data/reference-prices.json). findings.statement: Median top-10 holder share is 99.79% across the eight mints (99.86% SPX3L, 99.93% SPX3S, 99.20% TSL2L, 99.95% SOX3S, 99.72% SOX3L, 99.92% TSL1S, and the lower 81.39% SPCX2L and 95.78% SPCX2S), so the 1,810 reported holder accounts do not measure distribution - essentially all supply sits in issuer or market-maker inventory wallets.

findings.quote: In extreme cases, some or all of the Series Assets may become unrecoverable.
findings.statement: Inter-Series segregation is asserted "To the maximum extent permitted by the LLC Act" and the FAQ says "The debts of one Series cannot legally affect another", but no insolvency or trust-recognition opinion is published for the RMI series structure or for the off-chain holding arrangement, and the Risk Disclosure concedes that on custodian insolvency "In extreme cases, some or all of the Series Assets may become unrecoverable." A potentially confusing source: Shift publishes a page titled "Bankruptcy Remote Structure" and it is about a DIFFERENT product. It concerns Shift Vaults, where "all loans made via Shift are made to a single Borrower, OpenTrade SPC, a segregated portfolio company registered in the Cayman Islands" which "has been designed to be 'bankruptcy remote'" and where lenders are "secured creditors of the Borrower in a default event". None of that touches the leveraged Series tokens: there is no Cayman SPC, no independent board, no FCA-regulated operator and no security interest anywhere in the Series structure, which is why bankruptcyRemote stays null and securityInterest.exists stays false here.

findings.quote: holding the Tokens does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets
findings.statement: On the issuer's own site-wide notice the holder has no proprietary claim: holding the tokens "does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets". The Series agreements reinforce the downside - dissolution distributes only "after settling all debts", and cessation of member status, including involuntary withdrawal, "does not give rise to any right of a Member to a distribution of any property or economic resources". No security interest, trustee or collateral agent exists.

findings.quote: IV.3 No fiduciary duties unless expressly approved. In accordance with §109 of the DAO Act, no Member shall have any fiduciary duty to the Company or any Member unless otherwise provided for in this Agreement or any governance rules approved in accordance with this Agreement.
findings.statement: SHIFT DAO LLC is the issuer of every Series, its sole administrator, the party that "shall define which asset the Series acquires and holds", the recipient of an undisclosed percentage-of-treasury fee, and the holder of every on-chain authority. The only other parties in the agreements are a nominee member with "no economic entitlement or discretionary authority" and an unnamed "private entity that holds the backing assets"; the docs also state the Master DAO "does not serve as a manager, investment adviser, or fiduciary", so no independent party assures anything about the reserve or the register.

findings.quote: This requires timely and accurate reconciliation between on-chain token activity and off-chain activity, including acquisitions and disposals of off-chain assets linked to new issuances or redemptions.
findings.statement: The Risk Disclosure commits each Series to the obligation - "This requires timely and accurate reconciliation between on-chain token activity and off-chain activity, including acquisitions and disposals of off-chain assets linked to new issuances or redemptions" - and warns that failure "may result in imbalances". No reconciliation report, supply endpoint or per-Series holdings figure has ever been published, so the claim cannot be tested from outside.

findings.quote: These interests do not constitute public securities under RMI law, but purchasers are responsible for assessing their legal status in their jurisdiction.
findings.statement: A real company-law registration is presented alongside express denials of regulated status. The Terms of Use lean on the RMI DAO LLC registration for "legal clarity" while stating the interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law", and the site notice adds that the issuer "is not registered or authorized as an investment company under the U.S. Investment Company Act of 1940 ... and is not authorized as an Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), an Undertaking for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS), or an investment firm under the laws of any EEA Member State". A series vehicle that holds an ETF against redeemable interests is fund-shaped; no fund authorisation exists anywhere.

The mints themselves were created on 2026-05-12 to 2026-06-11 by HJfhNwwaDqcUc7k5J8N5y3y1xHZ7qDYMsC7YFpp9fCdp with a plain createAccount + initialize* + setAuthority script. links.label: Ownership of the underlying

fields.value: On paper: a membership interest in a designated Series of SHIFT DAO LLC whose sole purpose is to "acquire, hold, and maintain in its treasury assets whose economic performance corresponds to" one named index or stock. The Series 17 agreement says "Series 17 Members are owners in the Series 17 Assets" and Art. IV.1 says "Series Members are granted treasury ownership only", with no voting, management or fiduciary rights. In practice three things break that chain. (1) The issuer's own site-wide legal notice says the opposite: "The Series tokens provide their holders with economic exposure to the value of the Series Assets; holding the Tokens does not grant dividend rights, voting power, legal title, or claims to the underlying Series Assets." (2) The executed Series agreements do not identify the token they govern - membership is obtained by holding a token "created from and constricted by the parameters defined in the Smart Contract located at an address and a blockchain to be determined" - so no published document links the SPL mint that trades on Jupiter to the Series whose treasury holds the asset; the Series 17 (S&P 500) agreement compounds this by requiring "at least one (1) TSLA Short SHFT Token". (3) What the Series is documented to hold is not the referenced equity but a daily-reset leveraged ETF share (Series 17: SPXL, Direxion Daily S&P 500 Bull 3x, ISIN US25459W8626; Series 12: Direxion Daily TSLA X2, ISIN US25460G2865), so exposure to Tesla or the S&P 500 is delivered through a third party's derivative fund. Graded as derivative for that reason; if the Series agreements' "owners in the Series Assets" language controlled and were bound to these mints, the record would move to spv-claim-redeemable.

Two custodians are named, in the Risk Disclosure only: "Each Series relies on DekaBank, a European regulated financial institution, and ALPACADB LTD, a U.S.-regulated broker, as custodians of the Series Assets." The Collateral & Custody page adds that backing is held "with FINRA-registered, SEC-regulated brokerage partners" in "dedicated accounts, separate from operational balances and from other clients' assets" and "off-balance-sheet". Marketing and press name Alpaca Markets as the brokerage rail. The holding entity itself is not named ("a private entity that holds the backing assets"), nor is the market maker that operates the B2B mint/burn endpoints, and no account, statement, holdings report or balance for any Series has been published.

Each Series Operating Agreement grants a member a redemption right: "If a Member wishes to transfer their token back to the Series in exchange for funds, this is an internal membership-interest repurchase ... This transaction is available only to Members processed by smart contract where the transaction is settled directly from the treasury to the Member's wallet, not using any third-party assets." The Technical Overview says the opposite: "End users do not interact with the mint endpoint directly. Mint and burn are B2B endpoints used by professional market makers to maintain inventory. Users acquire Series Tokens by swapping on Jupiter against market-maker liquidity." U.S. and U.K. persons are excluded from membership entirely.

Documented retail path: internal membership-interest repurchase settled from the Series treasury by smart contract. Documented operational path: market makers mint and burn against the underlying ETF through B2B endpoints, 24/5 in line with U.S. trading hours, while user-facing trading is 24/7 RFQ on Jupiter, Meteora, Kamino and Orca. No burn address, latency, SLA or minimum is published for either path, and no SHIFT program exists on-chain to implement the smart-contract repurchase.

Primary market: "The per-token purchase price shall equal the executed market price paid in a bona fide transaction to acquire one (1) share of [the named ETF], plus a transaction fee equal to 0.1% of such executed price." Ongoing: "The Master DAO is allowed to charge operational fees to the Series using a percentage-of-treasury formula" - the percentage is never stated in the master or any Series agreement. Secondary market: "User-facing trading costs are reflected in the RFQ spread quoted by market makers", tightest in U.S. hours and widest at weekends; the two docs pages give different weekend ceilings ("up to ~3%" in Solution Overview, "up to ~5%" in Risk Management). No transfer fee is charged on-chain: none of the eight mints carries a transferFeeConfig extension.

links.label: Regulatory permission and disclosure

fields.value: Unregistered and self-disclaiming, on top of a real company-law registration. The site-wide legal notice states the tokens "have not been registered under the U.S. Securities Act of 1933 ... or under the securities or financial-instrument laws of any other jurisdiction", that the issuer "is not registered or authorized as an investment company under the U.S. Investment Company Act of 1940 ... and is not authorized as an Alternative Investment Fund (AIF), an Undertaking for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS), or an investment firm under the laws of any EEA Member State", and that the tokens are "not offered, sold, or distributed in the United States or the United Kingdom, nor to any U.S. or U.K. persons or entities; in applicable jurisdictions they are offered only to 'qualified investors,' 'professional clients,' or their equivalent legal analogues". The Terms of Use add that the membership interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law, but purchasers are responsible for assessing their legal status in their jurisdiction". No prospectus, offering document or exemption filing was located in any jurisdiction, and no licence for the Series tokens - but a licence CLAIM does exist, on a different product's page. The vaults-only Terms state: "Shift DAO LLC is a corporate entity in RMI with an international investment business license and registration number 10246-26.", with a Majuro registered address (PO Box 852, Long Island Rd) and physical address (852 Lagoon Rd). Three things qualify it. (1) SCOPE: that page governs Shift Vaults - stablecoin staking and secured lending to a Cayman SPC - not the leveraged Series tokens in this dossier, and no licence claim appears in any Series Operating Agreement, in the Terms of Use, in the Risk Disclosure or in the site-wide legal notice, all of which instead deny registered or authorised status. (2) VERIFICATION: the number could not be checked against any Marshall Islands register - no public searchable register of RMI international investment business licences was located - so it is recorded as unverified, not as false. (3) CONSISTENCY: an investment-business licence, if real, would sit oddly beside the same issuer's statement that the interests "do not constitute public securities under RMI law".

Laws of the Republic of the Marshall Islands, stated in both the Terms of Use (s.12) and each Series Operating Agreement (Art. XII.2). Recourse is narrow: after a 30-day notice period a dispute "shall be settled by arbitration administered by the International Centre for Dispute Resolution", seated in the RMI, sole arbitrator, English, final and without appeal, and "No action at law or in equity based upon any claim arising out of or related to this Agreement shall be instituted in any court of any jurisdiction". The Terms of Use separately submit website disputes to "the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of RMI". Members owe and are owed no fiduciary duty (Art. IV.3, DAO Act s.109), and under Art. VI.2 (DAO Act s.111) "no one shall have the right under the LLC Act to demand to separately inspect or copy records" of the Series. A THIRD regime exists on the same issuer's vaults-only Terms, and it differs from both of the above: arbitration is "finally settled under the Rules of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce by one or more arbitrators appointed in accordance with the said Rules", with the seat "agreed by the parties" rather than fixed in the RMI, the same RMI governing law "without regard to its conflict of law principles", and - unlike the Series agreements - an express class waiver: "You agree that any disputes will be resolved on an individual basis, and you waive any right to participate in a class action lawsuit or class-wide arbitration." So one legal entity operates three inconsistent dispute regimes: ICDR with an RMI seat and a total court bar for a Series member, ICC with a negotiable seat and a class waiver for a vaults depositor, and the exclusive jurisdiction of the RMI courts for a website user. The Series agreements contain no class or consolidation provision at all, so collective redress there is unaddressed rather than waived - though sole-arbitrator bilateral arbitration reaches the same result.
